Related Information
Inventory Counting
Manually Entering Counting Results
Posting Counting Results
 Note
We recommend that you follow the standard practice of creating an inventory counting document first and then posting the
counting results.
If you skip the step of creating a base inventory counting document, inventory records in the system are automatically adjusted
after you add an inventory posting document. If you make any mistake entering your counting results in the inventory posting
document, you have to make manual adjustments afterwards to correct the inventory records.
You have two ways to post your counting results based on one or more inventory counting documents:
Copy-to method: Open an existing inventory counting document and copy it to a new inventory posting document.
For more information, see Copy To Method.
Copy-from method: Open or create an inventory posting document and copy from one or more inventory counting
documents.
For more information, see Copy From Method.
Copy Options for Multiple Counters
For multiple counters, either the copy-to or copy-from method copies only one set of counting results to the inventory posting
document. For example, if you choose to post the team counting results or an individual counter's counting results, only the
specified set of counting results is copied.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 241

6/8/26, 6:08 AM
Depending on the counting type and selected counters, the following copy options are available:
Items with No Counters' Diff.: The system copies only items for which all counting results are the same.
Total Counted Qty: The system copies the sum of all team counters' counted quantities for each item.
<Individual Counter> - Counted Qty: The system copies the specified individual counter's counted quantity for each item.
Prerequisites
To have counting results in a specific row of an inventory counting document copied to the inventory posting document, the
following requirements must be met:
You have selected the Counted checkbox in the row.
The counted quantity you intend to copy is different from the in-warehouse quantity recorded in the system.
After Posting Counting Results
After you add an inventory posting document based on inventory counting documents, rows that are copied to the inventory
posting document are automatically closed and items in these rows are "unfrozen". However, some rows may remain open
because there is no difference between the in-warehouse quantity and the counted quantity. You cannot create new inventory
counting documents for the items recorded in the open rows. Similarly, items in the open rows remain "frozen" and you cannot
record any inventory transaction for them. To solve these issues, you must go back to your base inventory counting documents

Valuation Rules for Inventory Variances
 Note
The valuation rules for inventory opening balances are similar to the following rules for inventory variances.
Through an inventory counting, you may detect quantity variances of an item at different levels: at the bin-location level or at the
warehouse level. For example, there may be variances in several bin locations, but the variances cancel out each other at the
warehouse level. Depending on the valuation method of each item, there may be different rules for inventory valuation and
document fields.
Valuation Method: Standard, Moving Average, FIFO
If an item is stored in different bin locations of a warehouse, the variances of the item across the warehouse are consolidated first
and then the overall variance is used to determine gains or losses. As a natural result, if an item has variances in different bin
locations within the same warehouse, but the variances cancel out each other, there is no change in the inventory value of this item
and no journal entry is posted for it.
When the overall variance is negative, it indicates a loss, and the item cost is used to evaluate the change in the inventory value.
Depending on your setting, the item cost may be calculated per company or per warehouse; nevertheless, the system always
calculates inventory values and inventory value changes at the warehouse level.
As its name suggests, the Actual Price field always displays the item cost actually used to measure the change in the inventory
value: Change in Inventory Value = Actual Price × Overall Variance. If an item is stored in different bin locations of a warehouse,
the actual price may or may not be the same as the value in the Price field.

Valuation Method: Serial/Batch
 Note
For the sake of simplicity, we can treat an item managed by serial numbers as a special batch-managed item. Each unit of a
serial-managed item is one "batch" containing only one unit.
If an item is managed by the serial/batch valuation method and stored in a warehouse with bin locations, its receiving and issuing
transactions in an inventory posting or inventory opening balance document are handled separately. Issuing transactions are
consolidated based on the current cost, while receiving transactions are consolidated based on specified prices.
Compared with the other valuation methods, this rule means that there is not an overall variance for items managed by the
serial/batch valuation method. Instead, an item may have one overall negative variance and several consolidated positive
variances. The overall negative variance is valuated by the actual price of issued batches; each consolidated positive variance is
valuated by a different price that is specified by you.
In addition, for the same item, negative variances brought by issuing transactions are always valuated first.

Example: Standard Valuation Method
The examples below illustrate the valuation of inventory variances for items managed by the standard valuation method. They are
based on the following assumptions:
The system currency and the local currency are the same.
Bin locations B001 and B002 are in the same warehouse.
Item I001 is managed by the standard valuation method and its price is 10.
There are 2 units of item I001 in bin location B001 and 3 units of item I001 in bin location B002.
Current inventory value = 2 × 10 + 3 × 10 = 50

Negative variances and positive variances are not consolidated even if the cost and the price are the same. Therefore, there are two
rows in the audit report.
The negative variance (row 1) is posted first, as reflected in the first row of the audit report. The variances in row 2 and row 3 are
summed up and posted together, as reflected in the second row of the audit report.

General Area Fields
Count Date, Time
If you copy counting results from inventory counting documents with the same count date and time, these two fields display the
count date and time of the copied inventory counting documents and are disabled for editing. If you copy counting results from
multiple inventory counting documents with different count dates and times, these fields become empty and are disabled for
editing.
If you have set the system to calculate in-warehouse quantities on the count date according to transaction posting dates, you
cannot record the count time. In addition, transactions recorded on the count date may or may not be taken into consideration,
depending on your setting in the Document Settings window. Furthermore, as long as an inventory posting document remains as
a draft, every time you open the document, the system asks for your confirmation to recalculate in-warehouse quantities on the
count date. For more information, see Calculation of In-Warehouse Quantities on Count Date.
Price Source
You can take prices from the following three sources:
By Price List - The Price List field appears. Select the required price list from the list.
Last Evaluated Price - This is only relevant if a warehouse valuation report was previously generated.
Item Cost
If the variance is negative (the counted quantity is lower than the in-warehouse quantity), the system always displays the current
item cost in the Price field. In other words, the variance in the inventory value (Total field) posted to the journal entry is calculated
according to the item cost (counted quantity variance * item cost).
 Note
The journal entry for the document takes the item cost at the point of posting and this may not be the same as the cost
displayed in the Price field. This can happen if the item cost has changed between the time of adding the item to the document
and the time of adding the document itself, for example, because you have recorded some more purchases that use different
prices.

Available only if you have enabled multiple branches for this company. The branch information in each row is for reference
purposes and cannot be edited. For more information, see Working with Multiple Branches.

Referenced Document (<Number of Documents That the Current Document Refers To>)
Choose to open the Reference Information window. In this window, you can specify the reference documents for the current
document and view the documents that reference the current document.
Document Referenced To tab:
Lets you specify other documents across different business modules as the reference documents for your current
document. The types of other documents and your current one can be either the same or different.
Document Referenced By tab:
Lets you see which documents are using the current document as a reference
To specify Document B1 as a reference document for Document A1, proceed as follows:
1. Go to the Document Referenced To tab of Document A1.
2. Choose Transact. Type and select the document type of Document B1.
The supported documents are those with the Referenced Document function in their respective windows. For example,
journal entries, landed costs and incoming payments are unavailable here.
3. In the Doc. Number field, specify the document number B1.
4. Choose Update.
5. Document B1 appears on the Document Referenced To tab of Document A1. Accordingly, Document A1 appears on the
Document Referenced By tab of Document B1.
After you add the document, you can view and keep track of the reference relationships in the Relationship Map.
In addition, if you use the Duplicate option in the context menu or the Data menu in the menu bar to duplicate a marketing
document, you will see a message: Do you want to create a reference between the original and duplicate
documents? If you confirm the message, the original document is automatically set as a referenced document. You can view the
reference relationship through both the Reference Information window and the relationship map.
If you duplicate any document with existing document references, the document references are automatically copied from the
original document to its duplicate by default.
To cancel copying document references from original documents to their duplicates, go to the SAP Business One Main Menu
Administration System Initialization Document Settings General tab, and deselect the checkbox Copy Document
References from Original Documents to Duplicates.
 Note
The Copy To functionality does not copy the reference links, as the references are specific to the document for which they are

Copy from Inventory Counting
Displays a list of inventory counting documents for copying to the inventory posting document. After you select the inventory
counting documents to copy, the draw document wizard starts. Follow the wizard steps to add counting results from selected
inventory counting documents.
If there is no difference on a row between the counted quantities and the in-warehouse quantity recorded in the system, this row in
the inventory counting document may or may not be automatically closed after you add the inventory posting document. This
depends on your setting in the Document Settings window for inventory counting documents. For more information, see
Document Settings: Per Document Tab.
Note that you cannot select to copy two inventory counting documents with different counting types (multiple counters or a single
counter) for a single inventory posting document.

Exclude Bin Locations for Items with Zero Quantity
Some bin locations in a warehouse may not necessarily store an item, or the quantity of the item is currently recorded as zero in
the system. If you want to exclude from selection items with a zero quantity in these bin locations, select this checkbox.
If the counting results reveal that an item does exist in a bin location that has been excluded, you can manually add a row in the
document to record the discrepancy between the system and the actual storage.
Note that if your company allows negative inventory, and the quantity of an item falls below 0 in a bin location, the item in this bin
location is not excluded from selection.

Inventory Posting by Serial and Batch Number
In the inventory posting stage, SAP Business One lets you select serial and batch numbers for counted items, or adjust the
selection of serial and batch numbers that you made in inventory counting documents.
In inventory posting documents, the serial and batch numbers that were not selected as counted in inventory counting documents
are automatically selected to be issued from stock. The serial and batch numbers that were created as drafts in inventory counting
documents are converted into actual ones in the system.
Inventory Posting by Serial Number
If an item is counted by serial number, use this procedure to record the serial number information in inventory posting.
Prerequisites
You have entered the counted quantities for the items managed by serial numbers.
Procedure
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 258

6/8/26, 6:08 AM
1. Place the cursor in the rows of items managed by serial numbers and open the Serial Number Posting window in one of the
following ways:
Right-click and choose Serial and Batch Selection.
From the Go To menu, choose Serial and Batch Selection.
Place the cursor in the Counted Qty field, and press Ctrl and Tab .
2. In the table in the Available Serial Numbers section, choose the serial numbers that you do not find in warehouses after
the counting, and choose the right arrow button to move them to the Serial Numbers Difference section.
SAP Business One marks these items in red and issues them from stock after you add the inventory posting document.
3. If the serial numbers that you find in warehouses during counting do not exist in the system, that is, you do not see them in
the Available Serial Numbers section, choose the Create button to create new serial numbers.
SAP Business One marks these items in green and receives them to stock after you add the inventory posting document.
4. Choose the Update button.
 Example
For Item A in Whse 01, the quantity recorded in the system is 2, and the serial numbers are S01, S02. However, after
counting the inventory, you find that the quantity is 3, and the serial numbers are S01, S03, and S04.
In this case, you need to issue S02 from stock, and receive S03 and S04 to stock.
Proceed as follows:
1. Open the Serial Number Posting window.
2. Select S02, and move it to the Serial Numbers Difference section on the right. It will be marked in red.
3. Choose the Create button to create two new serial numbers S03 and S04. They will appear in green in the Serial
Numbers Difference section.
After an inventory posting document is added, you can review the transactions related to serial numbers in the serial number
transactions report in the following two ways:
Right-click the inventory posting document and choose Serial Number Transactions Report.
From the Go To menu, choose Serial Number Transactions Report.

 Note
SAP Business One supports approval processes and the function of saving documents as drafts for inventory opening

Valuation Rules for Inventory Variances
 Note
The valuation rules for inventory opening balances are similar to the following rules for inventory variances.
Through an inventory counting, you may detect quantity variances of an item at different levels: at the bin-location level or at the
warehouse level. For example, there may be variances in several bin locations, but the variances cancel out each other at the
warehouse level. Depending on the valuation method of each item, there may be different rules for inventory valuation and
document fields.
Valuation Method: Standard, Moving Average, FIFO
If an item is stored in different bin locations of a warehouse, the variances of the item across the warehouse are consolidated first
and then the overall variance is used to determine gains or losses. As a natural result, if an item has variances in different bin
locations within the same warehouse, but the variances cancel out each other, there is no change in the inventory value of this item
and no journal entry is posted for it.
When the overall variance is negative, it indicates a loss, and the item cost is used to evaluate the change in the inventory value.
Depending on your setting, the item cost may be calculated per company or per warehouse; nevertheless, the system always
calculates inventory values and inventory value changes at the warehouse level.
As its name suggests, the Actual Price field always displays the item cost actually used to measure the change in the inventory
value: Change in Inventory Value = Actual Price × Overall Variance. If an item is stored in different bin locations of a warehouse,
the actual price may or may not be the same as the value in the Price field.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 261

Valuation Method: Serial/Batch
  Note
For the sake of simplicity, we can treat an item managed by serial numbers as a special batch-managed item. Each unit of a
serial-managed item is one "batch" containing only one unit.
If an item is managed by the serial/batch valuation method and stored in a warehouse with bin locations, its receiving and issuing
transactions in an inventory posting or inventory opening balance document are handled separately. Issuing transactions are
consolidated based on the current cost, while receiving transactions are consolidated based on specified prices.
Compared with the other valuation methods, this rule means that there is not an overall variance for items managed by the
serial/batch valuation method. Instead, an item may have one overall negative variance and several consolidated positive
variances. The overall negative variance is valuated by the actual price of issued batches; each consolidated positive variance is
valuated by a different price that is specified by you.
In addition, for the same item, negative variances brought by issuing transactions are always valuated first.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 262

Example: Standard Valuation Method
The examples below illustrate the valuation of inventory variances for items managed by the standard valuation method. They are
based on the following assumptions:
The system currency and the local currency are the same.
Bin locations B001 and B002 are in the same warehouse.
Item I001 is managed by the standard valuation method and its price is 10.
There are 2 units of item I001 in bin location B001 and 3 units of item I001 in bin location B002.
Current inventory value = 2 × 10 + 3 × 10 = 50
Example 1: Overall Variance Negative
Add an inventory posting document with the following data:
Bin Location Counted Quantity Variance Price Actual Price Posted Value
| B001 | 3   | 1   | 15        | 10  | 10  |
| ---- | --- | --- | --------- | --- | --- |
| B002 | 1   | -2  | 10 (Cost) | 10  | -20 |
The journal entry looks like this:
| G/L Account                         |     | Debit |     | Credit |     |
| ----------------------------------- | --- | ----- | --- | ------ | --- |
| Inventory Account                   |     |       |     | 10     |     |
| Inventory Offset - Decrease Account |     | 10    |     |        |     |
Current inventory value = 10 × 3 + 10 × 1 = 40
Example 2: Overall Variance Positive
Add an inventory posting document with the following data:
Bin Location Counted Quantity Variance Price Actual Price Posted Value
| B001 | 4   | 2   | 15        | 10  | 20  |
| ---- | --- | --- | --------- | --- | --- |
| B002 | 2   | -1  | 10 (Cost) | 10  | -10 |
The journal entry looks like this:
| G/L Account                         |     | Debit |     | Credit |     |
| ----------------------------------- | --- | ----- | --- | ------ | --- |
| Inventory Offset - Increase Account |     |       |     | 15     |     |
| Inventory Account                   |     | 10    |     |        |     |
| Variance Account                    |     | 5     |     |        |     |
Current inventory value = 10 × 4 + 10 × 2 = 60
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 263

Inventory Audit Report
The inventory audit report displays two transactions:
| Quantity    | Cost | Transaction Value |     |     |     |     |
| ----------- | ---- | ----------------- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| -1 (Issue)  | 7    | -7                |     |     |     |     |
| 4 (Receipt) | 7    | 28                |     |     |     |     |
Negative variances and positive variances are not consolidated even if the cost and the price are the same. Therefore, there are two
rows in the audit report.
The negative variance (row 1) is posted first, as reflected in the first row of the audit report. The variances in row 2 and row 3 are
summed up and posted together, as reflected in the second row of the audit report.

Inventory Opening Balance Window
Use this window to define opening balances for inventory.
For more information, see Entering Inventory Opening Balances.
To access this window, from the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Inventory Transactions Inventory Opening
Balance .
 Note
This topic documents fields and other elements in this window that either are not self-explanatory or require additional
information.
General Area Fields
Posting Date
Displays the beginning date of the current fiscal year, by default. Once you change the posting date, the document date changes
accordingly.
Document Date
Displays the beginning date of the current fiscal year, by default. You can update the document date if necessary.
Price Source
You can take prices from the following three sources:
By Price List - The Price List field appears. Select the required price list from the list.
Last Evaluated Price - This is only relevant if a warehouse valuation report was previously generated.
Item Cost
If the variance is negative (the counted quantity is lower than the in-warehouse quantity), the system always displays the current
item cost in the Price field. In other words, the variance in the inventory value (Total field) posted to the journal entry is calculated
according to the item cost (counted quantity variance * item cost).
 Note
The journal entry for the document takes the item cost at the point of posting and this may not be the same as the cost
displayed in the Price field. This can happen if the item cost has changed between the time of adding the item to the document
and the time of adding the document itself, for example, because you have recorded some more purchases that use different
prices.

Inventory Revaluation
If your company runs a perpetual inventory system, you may need to perform inventory revaluation. Valuation is based on the
calculation methods Moving Average, Standard, FIFO, or Serial/Batch.
You can revaluate inventory values by:
Changing the price for a specific item
The inventory price is changed and inventory value is recalculated according to the new price.
Changing the value of a specific quantity of inventory
The quantity of inventory remains unchanged, resulting in a change in the price.
When inventory is subject to FIFO control and there are items in the FIFO layer, an inventory debit or credit results in a
posting to the inventory account. If the FIFO layer is empty, the posting goes to the price difference account.
 Note
You cannot perform inventory revaluation if any item involved is with a negative inventory value.
More Information

QR Codes and Inventory Transactions
QR (Quick Response) Codes can be displayed on marketing documents that are created by SAP Business One. QR Codes are
required by law on marketing documents in some jurisdictions. Companies can use QR Codes on marketing documents as a
convenient and customer-friendly way to provide more information.
QR Codes can link to anything that may be required but are typically a link to a webpage that displays information relevant to the
document.
Set up and Process
The following sections describe the set up and process in marketing documents for displaying QR Codes.
General Settings
A tab labeled QR Codes is available in General Settings. You can vary the technical details of QR Codes at the point of generation
by using the settings on QR Codes in General Settings. After changes are made in QR Codes in General Settings, the changes are
only effective for QR Codes if documents are updated or created.
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Administration System Initialization General Settings QR Codes
tab .
2. Determine the size of QR Codes by entering numbers between 1 and 40 in the fields Version - Min. Size and Max. Size. To
produce consistently sized QR Codes, you can enter the same number in both fields. Placing an upper limit on the size of
QR Codes restricts the amount of information that can be taken from the field Create QR Code From to create QR Codes.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 278

6/8/26, 6:08 AM
3. Enter a number between 1 and 20 in Scale (pixels per module) to determine how many pixels are in a square of a bitmap in
the PNG file.
4. Select the checkbox QR Code Expiration to automatically remove QR Codes from the database in a specified number of
days, entered in Expiration Days. Expiration dates are calculated and potentially recalculated from the last update of a
document.
5. Redundant correction bytes are included and vary by the chosen Correction Level of created QR Codes. Choosing a setting
of "High" means that less information can be included in the QR Code but that the QR Code can be read and printed more
easily with less potential for error. Choosing a setting of "Low" means that more information can be included in the QR
Code but that the QR Code can be read and printed less easily with more potential for error.
Marketing Documents
The field Create QR Code From is available on the Accounting tab of marketing documents, for example on Inventory Transfers.
The information entered in Create QR Code From is used as the source from which QR Codes are saved in system tables and
transformed into PNG (Portable Network Graphic) images. Information can be added manually to Create QR Code From, by using
a formula in a formatted search, by DI API input, or by SAP Business One Service Layer on Windows (not on Linux). The source for
QR Codes can also be user-defined fields that are called by API. The information entered into Create QR Code From can be
anything that customers require but is typically a link to a webpage that displays information relevant to the document. You can
display QR Code images on print layouts of marketing documents. Print layouts must be manually adjusted to include QR Code
images based on joined data sources in the system.
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Inventory Transactions Inventory Transfer .
2. Enter a link to a webpage for your company's inventory team in Create QR Code From.
3. Add the inventory transfer to the system to trigger the generation of a QR Code.
 Note
For more information on QR Codes, example queries, and Crystal Report files, see SAP Note 2889899 .

Working with Bin Locations
With SAP Business One, you can manage bin locations for your warehouses. In order to provide you with more flexibility in
inventory management, SAP Business One lets you enable the bin location function for individual warehouses.
After you enable the bin location function for intended warehouses, bin locations need to be recorded for all receipts and issues of
inventory in those warehouses, including the processing of the following documents or transactions:
Purchasing: goods receipt PO, goods return, A/P invoice, A/P credit memo.
Sales: delivery, return, A/R invoice, A/R invoice +payment, A/R credit memo.
Inventory: goods receipt, goods issue, inventory transfer, inventory opening balance, inventory counting, inventory posting,
pick and pack.
Production: receipt from production, issue for production.
Both the images in this topic are interactive and you can choose the highlighted areas for more information. In the first graphic,
you can understand the bin location-related tasks, for example, enabling and replenishing bin locations.
Please note that image maps are not interactive in PDF outputs.
The second graphic contains referential topics about bin locations. Choosing each tile directs you to a specific topic.
Please note that image maps are not interactive in PDF outputs.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 2

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
Bin Locations
A bin location is the smallest addressable unit of space in a warehouse where your goods are stored.
The following diagram shows you an example of a warehouse and its bin locations:
To help you work with bin locations in a more efficient manner, SAP Business One provides you with the following four kinds of bin
locations. Properly used, they can speed up the process of receipts and issues of inventory in your bin locations.
 Note
In SAP Business One, you can set a bin location as a receiving bin location and default bin location at the same time.
Receiving Bin Location – A special section in a warehouse which typically represents a receiving inspection area for
temporary storage of incoming goods. After the inspection is completed, the goods are then placed in the storage bin
locations.
To designate a bin location as a receiving bin location, select the Receiving Bin Location checkbox in the Bin Location
Master Data window.
SAP Business One can automatically place the incoming goods in the receiving bin locations of your warehouse if the
following conditions are met:
You have enabled receiving bin locations for your warehouse.
To do this, select the Enable Receiving Bin Locations checkbox on the General tab of the Warehouses – Setup
window.
There are active receiving bin locations in your warehouse.
For more information, see Automatic Bin Location Allocation in Receipts.
Storage Bin Location – A bin location in a warehouse where the goods are stored.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 3

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
To indicate a bin location is a storage bin location, leave the Receiving Bin Location checkbox in the Bin Location Master
Data window unselected.
Default Bin Location – A bin location which is used to store incoming goods by default. SAP Business One lets you specify
the default bin locations on the following three levels:
Warehouse
To specify the default bin location for all items in a warehouse, go to Warehouses - Setup: Bin Locations Tab.
Item Group
To specify the default bin location for all items in an item group, go to Item Groups - Setup.
Item
To specify the default bin location for an item, go to Item Master Data: Inventory Data Tab.
 Note
For an item, if you have specified the default bin locations on all three levels, the priority of the bin locations are as
follows:
Default Bin Location of Item > Default Bin Location of Item Group > Default Bin Location of Warehouse
During receipt of the item, the default bin location you've specified on the item level is considered the first choice among
the three default bin locations in terms of the storage location.
Typically, you can set a storage bin location as the default bin location for storing a particular item, or items from a
particular item group or warehouse. SAP Business One automatically allocates the incoming items to the default bin
location unless your warehouse has receiving bin locations.
For more information, see Automatic Bin Location Allocation in Receipts.
System Bin Location – A bin location predefined by SAP Business One for each warehouse which has enabled bin
locations. The bin location code is <Warehouse Code> <Bin Location Code Separator> SYSTEM-BIN-
LOCATION.
By default, the system bin location of a warehouse is set as the warehouse's default bin location. It's used for receiving and
issuing items automatically if it is the only bin location in the warehouse.
With the predefined system bin locations, you can carry out your regular transactions without having to create bin location-
related data immediately after enabling the function.
 Note
You cannot change, deactivate, or delete any system bin location.

Enter up to five characters as the separator of bin location codes. The characters can be alphabetic letters, numbers, symbols, or a

Each bin location code comprises several segments: the warehouse code and the warehouse sublevel codes. Once you have

Default Bin Location
Specify the default bin location in the warehouse for receiving items. By default, SAP Business One automatically creates a system
bin location for the warehouse once bin locations are enabled, and assigns the system bin location as the default bin location for
receiving items.
During receipt of items, the default bin location is automatically assigned for storing items.
 Note
If you have enabled receiving bin locations for the warehouse, then by default, the receiving bin locations are used
automatically to store the items received externally from your vendors or customers. The default bin locations are used
automatically only to store items received internally, for example, the items transferred from other warehouses or the finished
products collected from factories.
Enforce Default Bin Loc.
 Note
If you have not specified a default bin location, the checkbox is disabled.
Select the checkbox to enforce the use of the default bin location during receipt of items to the warehouse. That is, when you
receive an item to the warehouse, you must place it in the default bin location.
Exceptions:
You have specified a default bin location for the item group to which the item belongs.
You have specified a default bin location for the item.
Among the three default bin locations, the priority is as follows:
Default Bin Location of Item > Default Bin Location of Item Group > Default Bin Location of Warehouse
Therefore, if you have specified a default bin location for the item or item group, the enforced default bin location on the warehouse
level is not in effect.
Auto Alloc. on Issue
Select the method by which items are automatically allocated from bin locations during issue. You can select one of the following
methods:
Single Choice – Allocates items from bin locations when there is only one way of doing it. If there is more than one way to
allocate items from bin locations, the single choice method is not effective.
The single choice method is applicable only in one of the following situations:
The item you need to issue exists only in one bin location.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 8

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
In this case, there is no other way of issuing the item but from this bin location.
The item you need to issue exists in more than one bin location and the entire inventory of the item must be taken to
fulfill the requirement.
In this case, there is no other way of issuing the entire inventory of the item but from all the bin locations.
 Example
Example 1
You want to deliver item A with quantity 50 to a customer.
In your warehouse, you have 200 units of item A stored in bin location X.
In this case, even if your inventory greatly exceeds the committed quantity, you can pick 50 from bin location X.
If you select Single Choice as the method, SAP Business One automatically picks the items from bin location X for the
delivery.
Example 2
You want to deliver item B with quantity 100 to a customer.
In your warehouse, you have exactly 100 units of item B stored as follows:
Bin location Y: 60
Bin location Z: 40
In this case, you can pick 60 from bin location Y and 40 from bin location Z to fulfill the delivery.
If you select Single Choice as the method, SAP Business One automatically picks the items from the two bin locations
for the delivery.
Bin Location Code Order – Allocates items from bin locations according to the alphanumeric order of the bin location
codes
Alternative Sort Code Order – Allocates items from bin locations according to the alphanumeric order of the bin locations'
alternative sort codes
Descending Quantity – Allocates items from bin locations according to the descending order of the item quantity in the bin
locations
Ascending Quantity – Allocates items from bin locations according to the ascending order of the item quantity in the bin
locations
Ascending Quantity – Single Bin Preferred – Allocates items from a single bin location that fully satisfies the required
quantity. If more than one such bin location exists, the one with the least quantity is to be used.
If no single bin location satisfies the required quantity, the items are to be allocated from bin locations according to the
ascending order of the item quantity in the bin locations.
FIFO - Allocates items from bin locations according to the "First In, First Out" principle
LIFO - Allocates items from bin locations according to the "Last In, First Out" principle

Creating Bin Locations
Prerequisites
1. You have enabled bin locations for your warehouse.
For more information, see Enabling Bin Locations.
2. You have activated the warehouse sublevels and bin location attributes in Bin Location Field Activation Window.
3. You have defined the warehouse sublevel codes and bin location attribute codes.
To define the warehouse sublevel codes, go to Warehouse Sublevel Codes - Setup Window.
To define the bin location attribute codes, go to Bin Location Attribute Codes - Setup Window.
Context
After you have enabled bin locations for a warehouse, you can create bin locations for the warehouse.
SAP Business One can generate bin locations in batches automatically. Alternatively, you can create bin locations manually.
To manually create bin locations, use the bin location master data.
To access the Bin Location Master Data window, from the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Bin Locations
Bin Location Master Data .
To let SAP Business One generate bin locations for you, proceed as follows:
Procedure
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Bin Locations Bin Location Management .
The Bin Location Management window opens.
2. In the Management Task field, select Generate Bin Locations from the dropdown list.
3. In the Bin Location Codes section, specify the codes for the bin locations you want to generate.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 11

4. In the Bin Location Properties section, specify the properties for the bin locations you want to generate.
5. Choose the OK pushbutton.

expect to be generated.
 Note
If the bin locations cannot be generated due to certain conflicts with the system, you can see the detailed error
description in the Error Details column.
6. In the Bin Location Management – Generation Preview window, choose the Generate pushbutton.

Warehouse Sublevel Codes - Setup Window
Use this window to set up different codes for each warehouse sublevel.
With actual businesses, a big warehouse is often divided into several levels of subunits, and the lowest level of subunit is the actual
bin location where the goods are stored. In order to identify each bin location with a unique code, SAP Business One requires you
to use the codes of the warehouse and warehouse sublevels to compose the bin location codes.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 13

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
 Example
Warehouse A has the following levels of subunits:
Warehouse sublevel 1 – Wing
Sublevel codes – WINGEAST and WINGWEST, which refer to the east and west wings in the warehouse, respectively.
Warehouse sublevel 2 – Section
Sublevel codes – SECTIONA and SECTIONB, which represent section A and B in each wing.
Warehouse sublevel 3 – Shelf
Sublevel codes – SHELF01 and SHELF02, which stand for shelf 01 and 02 in each section.
Shelf is the smallest unit of space in the warehouse, which also represents the physical location of the bin.
To indicate the eight bin locations (shelves), SAP Business One lets you define the following bin location codes with the
warehouse and warehouse sublevel codes:
A-WINGEAST-SECTIONA-SHELF01
A-WINGEAST-SECTIONA-SHELF02
A-WINGEAST-SECTIONB-SHELF01
A-WINGEAST-SECTIONB-SHELF02
A-WINGWEST-SECTIONA-SHELF01
A-WINGWEST-SECTIONA-SHELF02
A-WINGWEST-SECTIONB-SHELF01
A-WINGWEST-SECTIONB-SHELF02
 Note
The separator - between the warehouse and warehouse sublevel codes is defined in Warehouses - Setup: Bin Locations
Tab. By default, the bin location code separator is a hyphen ”-”.
To access the window, from the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Administration Setup Inventory Bin Locations

Sublevel Code Segment From ... To
Specify the sublevel code segments which comprise the warehouse sublevel codes you want to generate. You can specify a range
for each segment.
Each warehouse sublevel code can consist of up to six segments, and each segment can be any of the following types:
Fixed – Any fixed string with a maximum length of 50 characters
You can enter alphabetic letters, numbers, symbols, or a combination of all. For a fixed string, you cannot specify a range.
Alphabetic – Alphabetic letters with a maximum length of 50 characters
 Note
When you specify a range, you must ensure the following:
The characters have the same length in the From and To fields.
The first letter in the From field must precede alphabetically the first letter in the To field.
Numeric – Numbers with a maximum length of 50 characters
 Note
When you specify a range, you must ensure the number in the From field is less than or equal to the number in the To field.
SAP Business One lets you enter numbers of different lengths in the From and To fields. In this case, while generating the
warehouse sublevel codes, SAP Business One automatically adds leading zeros to the number in the From field]
For example, if you enter 1 and 10 in the From and To fields respectively, SAP Business One automatically considers the range
as being from 01 to 10.
 Note
SAP Business One automatically applies upper case to any alphabetic letters you enter in these fields.
 Example
You have specified the following sublevel code segments:
Segment 1 – Fixed: ZONE
Segment 2 – Alphabetic: from A to B
Segment 3 – Numeric: from 1 to 02
As a result, the following warehouse sublevel codes are generated:
ZONEA01
ZONEA02
ZONEB01
ZONEB02

None – Indicates a bin location has no item restrictions, that is, the bin location can store any item.

 Note
Once you have put the single item in the bin location, you cannot place another kind of item in it unless either of the
following situations arises:
There is no inventory of the single item in the bin location.
There is negative inventory of the single item in the bin location.
In this case, if you place another kind of item in the bin location, SAP Business One still allows you to receive the
original single item till the quantity reaches zero.
Specific Item Group – Indicates a bin location is restricted to a specific item group, that is, the bin location can only store

view the UoM in the Current UoM field on the right side.

Once you have put one or more items with a single UoM in the bin location, you cannot place any item with another UoM
in it unless either of the following situations arises:
All items using the current UoM in the bin location have zero inventories.
Each item using this single UoM in the bin location has negative inventory.
In this case, if you place items with another UoM in the bin location, SAP Business One still allows you to receive
items with the original single UoM until the quantity for each item reaches zero.
Specific UoM Group – Indicates the bin location is restricted to a specific UoM group, that is, the bin location can only store
items with a specific UoM group.
To specify the UoM, select a UoM from the choose from list in the UoM Group field on the right side.
Single UoM Group Only – Indicates the bin location is restricted to a single UoM group, that is, the bin location can only
store items with the same UoM group.
You cannot specify which UoM group it is. The UoM group of the first item you put in the bin location becomes the single
UoM group. You can view the UoM group in the Current UoM Group field on the right side.

Bin Location Master Data
To facilitate bin location management, SAP Business One lets you maintain a master data record for each bin location. In the bin
location master data, you can define the following:
Bin Location Code
To identify each bin location with a unique code, SAP Business One requires you to use the codes of the warehouse and
warehouse sublevels to compose bin location codes as follows:
<Warehouse Code><Code Separator><Sublevel 1 Code><Code Separator><Sublevel 2 Code><Code
Separator><Sublevel 3 Code><Code Separator><Sublevel 4 Code>
 Example
Warehouse A has the following sublevels:
Warehouse sublevel 1 – Wing
Sublevel codes – WINGEAST and WINGWEST, which refer to the east and west wings in the warehouse,
respectively.
Warehouse sublevel 2 – Section
Sublevel codes – SECTIONA and SECTIONB, which represent section A and B in each wing.
Warehouse sublevel 3 – Shelf
Sublevel codes – SHELF01 and SHELF02, which stand for shelf 01 and 02 in each section.
Shelf is the smallest unit of space in the warehouse and also represents the physical location of the bin.
To indicate the eight bin locations (shelves), SAP Business One lets you define the following bin location codes with the
warehouse and warehouse sublevel codes:
 Note
The separators - between the warehouse and warehouse sublevel codes are defined in Warehouses - Setup: Bin
Locations Tab. By default, the bin location code separator is a hyphen ”-”.
A-WINGEAST-SECTIONA-SHELF01
A-WINGEAST-SECTIONA-SHELF02
A-WINGEAST-SECTIONB-SHELF01
A-WINGEAST-SECTIONB-SHELF02
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 24

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
A-WINGWEST-SECTIONA-SHELF01
A-WINGWEST-SECTIONA-SHELF02
A-WINGWEST-SECTIONB-SHELF01
A-WINGWEST-SECTIONB-SHELF02
 Note
When defining bin location codes, you can omit one or more sublevels, if required. For instance, in the above
example, you can also define the following valid bin location codes:
A-WINGEAST-SHELF01
A-SECTIONB-SHELF02
A-WINGWEST
A-SECTIONA
A-SHELF01
Bin Location Properties
For each bin location, SAP Business One lets you define a set of properties with which you can do the following:
Restrict the storage of your bin locations, for example, to a particular batch, item, or item group
Restrict the use of your bin locations, for example, to receiving or issuing goods only
Set up the minimum and maximum quantities of items for your bin locations, so that you can replenish the
inventory in the bin locations to the maximum when the inventory level falls below the minimum
 Note
The minimum and maximum quantities do not have any effect on the receipt or issue of inventory in your bin
locations. That is, SAP Business One does not block the receiving or issuing of items, even if it is causing the
inventory in your bin locations to exceed the maximum or fall below the minimum.
Define a number of attributes for your bin locations, for example, size, volume, temperature, or color
You can generate, update, and delete the bin locations in batches using bin location management.

Bin Location Master Data Window
Use this window to add, update and view the bin locations.
To access the window, from the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Bin Locations Bin Location Master Data .
General Area
Warehouse
From a choose from list of warehouses, select a warehouse where the bin is located.
The bin location code comprises the warehouse code, the sublevel codes, and the bin location code separator you defined.
<Sublevel 1> ... <Sublevel 4>
From a choose from list of warehouse sublevel codes, select the sublevel codes that represent the physical location of the bin.
The bin location code comprises the warehouse code, the sublevel codes, and the bin location code separator you defined.
 Note
Only the sublevels you have activated are available.
By default, SAP Business One activates sublevel 1 for you. To activate other warehouse sublevels, go to Bin Location Field
Activation Window.
Bin Location Code
Displays the code of the bin location.
The bin location code comprises the warehouse code, the sublevel codes, and the bin location code separator you specified.
Modify Bin Location Codes
Choose this button to open the Bin Location Code Modification window, where you can modify bin location codes in batches.
Manage Bin Locations
Choose this button to open the Bin Location Management window, where you can generate, update, and delete bin locations in
batches.
Bin Location Properties
Inactive
Deactivates the bin location.
Once a bin location is inactive, you cannot use the bin location for any purposes until you activate it again.
 Note
You can deactivate the bin location only if there is no inventory of any item in the bin location.
Receiving Bin Location
Select the checkbox to indicate the bin location is a receiving bin location.
A receiving bin location is within a special section in a warehouse which typically represents a receiving inspection area for
temporary storage of incoming goods. After the inspection is completed, the goods are then placed in storage bin locations.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 26

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
Once you enable receiving bin locations for a warehouse and designate a bin location in the warehouse as a receiving bin location,
this bin location is used automatically to store the items received externally from your vendors or customers.
Exclude from Auto. Alloc. On Issue
Select this checkbox to exclude the current bin location from those bin locations from which items are automatically allocated
during issue.
Description
If required, enter a description of the bin location.
Item Weight
Displays the total weight of the items held in the bin location, using the weight defined on the Inventory Data tab in the Item
Master Data window. However, items with negative quantities held in the bin location are not included.
Item Qty
Displays the total quantity of items in the bin location.
To view the details of the items, open the bin location content list by clicking to the left of the quantity.
No. of Items
Displays how many kinds of items are stored in the bin location.
No. of Batches/Serials
Displays how many serials and batches are stored in the bin location.
To view the details of the serials and batches, open the bin location content list by clicking to the left of the number.
Alternative Sort Code
If required, enter an alternative sort code for the bin location. The code can be alphabetic letters, numbers, symbols, or a
combination of all. You can enter up to 50 characters.
During the inventory issue, the system can use the code as a criteria to decide from which bin locations items are allocated.
 Note
SAP Business One automatically applies upper case to any alphabetic letters you enter.
Bar Code
If required, enter a bar code for the bin location. The code can be alphabetic letters, numbers, symbols, or a combination of all. You
can enter up to 100 characters.
Minimum Qty
Enter the minimum quantity of items for the bin location.
When the inventory level in a bin location falls below the minimum quantity, you can replenish the bin location to the maximum
quantity using either of the following two reports:
Bin location list
Bin location content list
 Note
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 27

The minimum quantity does not have any effect on the issues of inventory from the bin location. That is, SAP Business One
does not block the issuing of items even if it is causing the inventory in the bin location to fall below the minimum quantity.
Maximum Qty
Enter the maximum quantity of items for the bin location.
When the inventory level of a bin location falls below the minimum quantity, you can replenish the bin location to the maximum
quantity using either of the following two reports:
Bin location list
Bin location content list
 Note

checkbox is not effective for the current bin location, even if you have selected it.

If you do not define a maximum weight, or you define the maximum weight as zero, then the Receive Up to Max. Weight
checkbox is not effective for the current bin location, even if you have selected it.

Updating Bin Location Properties
Prerequisites
You have enabled bin locations for your warehouse.
For more information, see Enabling Bin Locations.
Context
After you have enabled and created bin locations for a warehouse, you can update the properties of the bin locations.
SAP Business One can update bin locations in batches automatically. Alternatively, you can also manually update bin locations.
To manually update bin location properties, use the bin location master data.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 31

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
To access the Bin Location Master Data window, from the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Bin Locations
Bin Location Master Data .
To let SAP Business One update bin location properties for you, proceed as follows:
Procedure
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Bin Locations Bin Location Management .
The Bin Location Management window opens.
2. In the Management Task field, select Update Bin Location Properties from the dropdown list.
3. In the Select Bin Locations section, select a range of bin locations that you want to update.
4. In the Specify Properties to Update for Selected Bin Locations section, select the properties that you want to update and
specify the new properties.
5. Choose the OK pushbutton.
The Bin Location Management – Update Preview window opens, where you can preview the bin locations with the
expected properties.
 Note
If the bin location properties cannot be updated due to certain conflicts with the system, you can see the detailed error
description in the Error Details column.
6. In the Bin Location Management – Update Preview window, choose the Update pushbutton.

items with a specific UoM group.
To specify the UoM, select a UoM from the choose from list in the UoM Group field on the right side.
Single UoM Group Only – Indicates the bin location is restricted to a single UoM group, that is, the bin location can only
store items with the same UoM group.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 35

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
You cannot specify which UoM group it is. The UoM group of the first item you put in the bin location becomes the single
UoM group. You can view the UoM group in the Current UoM Group field on the right side.
 Note
Once you have put one or more items with a single UoM group in the bin location, you cannot place any item with
another UoM group in it unless either of the following situations arises:
All items using the current UoM group in the bin location have zero inventories.
Each item using this single UoM group in the bin location has negative inventory.
In this case, if you place items with another UoM group in the bin location, SAP Business One still allows you to
receive items with the original single UoM group until the quantity for each item reaches zero.
Batch Restrictions
If you want to update the batch restriction status of the selected bin locations, select the left-side checkbox first.
Then, select either of the following options in the right-side field to indicate the batch restriction status of the selected bin
locations:
None – Indicates a bin location has no batch restrictions, that is, the bin location can store any items regardless of its batch
information.
Single Batch – Indicates a bin location is restricted to a single batch, that is, the bin location can only store items from one
batch.
You cannot specify which batch it is. The batch of the first item you put in the bin location becomes the single batch. Later,
you can view the batch in the Current Batch field in the Bin Location Master Data window.
 Note
If you restrict a bin location to a single batch, you cannot store non-batch items in the bin location.
Once you have put a batch in the bin location, you cannot place another batch in it until the inventory of the existing
batch reduces to zero.
Transaction Restrictions
If you want to update the transaction restriction status of the selected bin locations, select the left-side checkbox first.
Then, select one of the following options in the right-side field to indicate the transaction restriction status of the selected bin
locations:
None – Indicates a bin location has no transaction restrictions, that is, the bin location can be used in any relevant
transactions.
All Transactions – Indicates a bin location is restricted from all transactions, that is, the bin location cannot be used in any
transactions.
Inbound Transactions – Indicates a bin location is restricted from inbound transactions, that is, the bin location cannot be
used to store any incoming flow of goods.
Outbound Transactions – Indicates a bin location is restricted from outbound transactions, that is, the bin location cannot
be used during the issuing of goods.
 Note

All Except Inventory Transfer and Counting – Indicates the bin location is restricted to inventory transfer, counting and
posting only. That is, the bin location can only be used during inventory transfer, counting and posting.

Modifying Bin Location Codes
Prerequisites
You have enabled bin locations for your warehouse.
For more information, see Enabling Bin Locations.
Context
In the course of warehouse reorganization, the warehouse sublevels are often adjusted and the bin locations restructured. Since
SAP Business One requires you to use the codes of the warehouse and warehouse sublevels to compose the bin location codes,
you may need to modify the bin location codes as a result of the reorganization.
In SAP Business One, you can modify the bin location codes one by one or in batches. Once you have successfully changed a
source bin location code to a target bin location code, SAP Business One automatically transfers the inventory from the source bin
location to the target bin location and deactivates the source bin location.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 37

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
With the bin location code modification, you can do the following:
Changing a source bin location code to a target bin location code
Changing a range of source bin location codes into one target bin location code
In this case, SAP Business One transfers the inventory from all source bin locations to the target bin location and
deactivates all source bin locations.
Changing a range of source bin location codes to a range of target bin location codes
 Note
As every bin location code is unique in SAP Business One, you must merge the bin location codes when either of the following
conditions arises:
The target bin location code already exists.
In this case, you must merge the source bin location code with the existing target bin location code.
Multiple source bin location codes share one target bin location code.
In this case, you must merge all source bin location codes into one.
To merge bin location codes, select the Merge Bin Location Codes checkbox in the Bin Location Code Modification – Preview
window.
If the target bin location code does not exist, SAP Business One automatically creates the target bin location with the same
properties as those of the source bin location.
However, in case you change a range of source bin location codes into a target bin location code that does not exist, the target
bin location is created with the same properties as those of the first bin location in the source range.
Procedure
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Bin Locations Bin Location Code Modification .
The Bin Location Code Modification window opens.
2. In the Select Bin Location Codes section, select a range of bin location codes that you want to modify.
3. In the Modify Sublevels for Selected Bin Location Codes, select the sublevel code segments you want to modify and
specify the new sublevel codes.
 Note
To remove a sublevel code segment from the selected bin location codes, select the checkbox on the left side of the
sublevel and leave the field on the right side empty.
4. Choose the OK pushbutton.
The Bin Location Code Modification – Preview window opens, where you can preview the target bin location codes.
5. In the Bin Location Management – Update Preview window, select the bin location codes you want to modify, specify
whether you allow the merge of bin location codes, and choose the Modify pushbutton.
 Note
If the source bin location codes cannot be modified due to certain conflicts with the target bin location codes, SAP
Business One marks the rows in red. You can see the detailed error description in the Error Details column.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 38

Deleting Bin Locations
Prerequisites
You have enabled bin locations for your warehouse.
For more information, see Enabling Bin Locations.
Context
 Note
You can delete a bin location only if it has not been used in any settings, documents or transactions.
You cannot delete a system bin location.
In case you have accidentally created bin locations with the wrong information, SAP Business One lets you delete the bin locations.
SAP Business One can delete bin locations in batches automatically. Alternatively, you can delete bin locations manually.
To manually delete bin locations, do the following:
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Bin Locations Bin Location Master Data .
2. Find the bin location that you want to delete.
3. In the Bin Location Master Data window, do one of the following:
Right-click and choose Remove.
In the menu bar, choose Data Remove .
To let SAP Business One delete the bin locations for you, proceed as follows:
Procedure
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Bin Locations Bin Location Management .
The Bin Location Management window opens.
2. In the Management Task field, select Delete Bin Locations from the dropdown list.
3. In the Select Bin Locations section, select a range of bin locations that you want to delete.
4. In the Expanded Selection Criteria section, specify the properties of the bin locations you want to delete to further narrow
down the bin location range.
5. Choose the OK pushbutton.
The Bin Location Management – Deletion Preview window opens, where you can preview the bin locations that you expect
to be deleted.
 Note
If the bin locations cannot be deleted, you can see the detailed error description in the Error Details column.
6. In the Bin Location Management – Deletion Preview window, choose the Delete pushbutton.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 44

If you want to filter the bin locations by their attributes, select the checkboxes to the left of the intended attribute fields first.
Then, enter the attribute codes in the right-side attribute fields. SAP Business One automatically searches through the selected
bin locations and finds those with the specified attributes.
If you leave the attribute fields empty, SAP Business One filters out all selected bin locations which have specified an attribute
code in these fields.

Context
In SAP Business One, you can set up the minimum and maximum quantities of items for your bin locations in the bin location
master data. With the minimum and maximum quantities, you can replenish the inventory in your bin locations to the maximum if
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 49

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
the inventory level falls below the minimum.
To replenish the inventory in a bin location, you can create receipt documents. Alternatively, you can transfer inventory from other
bin locations to this one through either of the following reports:
Bin location list
Bin location content list
 Note
SAP Business One lets you replenish the inventory in a bin location using the above two reports only when the bin location
meets either of the following conditions:
The bin location contains a single item and the item quantity is not zero.
The bin location is restricted to a specific item and the item quantity is zero.
Only in the above situations can the system decide which item to replenish in a bin location.
In the two reports, you can get an overview of the inventory status in your bin locations from the following two columns:
Qty Below Min. – Indicates whether the inventory level in the bin location falls below the minimum quantity you defined.
The quantity is calculated with the following formula:
Qty Below Min. = Minimum Qty – Item Qty
Replenishment Qty – Displays how many items you are recommended to replenish in the bin location.
The quantity is calculated with the following formula:
Replenishment Qty = Maximum Qty – Item Qty
 Note
Note the following:
For the bin location content list, if you select the Display Batch/Serial Numbers checkbox, the Qty Below Min. and
Replenishment Qty are not calculated.
The calculation of the replenishment quantity is independent from the calculation of the quantity below the minimum.
Even if a bin location’s Qty Below Min is negative, which means the inventory level of the bin location is above the
minimum, the Replenishment Qty is calculated nevertheless. In this case, you can still choose to replenish the inventory
for the bin location.
To replenish the inventory in your bin locations using the bin location list or the bin location content list, proceed as follows:
Procedure
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose either of the following:
Inventory Inventory Reports Bin Location List
Inventory Inventory Reports Bin Location Content List
2. In the Bin Location List - Selection Criteria or Bin Location List - Selection Criteria window, specify the selection criteria
and choose OK.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 50

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
3. In the Bin Location List or Bin Location Content List window, select the checkboxes for the bin locations you want to
replenish.
 Note
For a more convenient selection of the bin locations, use the SAP Business One sort feature by double-clicking any
column header.
For example, if you just want to replenish the bin locations whose inventory level has dropped below the minimum
quantities, you can sort the Qty Below Min. column and select the bin locations with a positive Qty Below Min. only.
4. Choose the Bin Location Transfer pushbutton, and select Replenish Bin Locations from the opened list.
The Inventory Transfer window opens, where the selected bin locations are on the receiving end of the document. SAP
Business One automatically checks the existing bin locations which contain the items that are going to be replenished, and
picks the issuing bin locations among them according to the automatic allocation methods of the warehouses.
 Note
While searching for bin locations that contain the items that are going to be replenished, SAP Business One
automatically filters out those bin locations which you have selected for replenishment.
For example, you want to replenish the inventory of item A to 100 in bin location X, and bin location X already has 50
units of A in stock. While SAP Business One tries to find out from which bin locations the required 50 units can be
issued, it immediately eliminates A from the possibility of replenishing itself.
5. After you confirm all information, choose Add in the Inventory Transfer window.

Automatic Bin Location Allocation in Receipts
To facilitate bin location allocation during inventory receipts, SAP Business One makes it possible to automate the process of
allocating received items to bin locations.
The automatic bin location allocation process can take place with all documents that involve the receiving of items. For a list of
receipt documents, see Receipts to Bin Locations.
 Note
The automatic bin location allocation rules in the following sections are the general rules applied to all receipt documents.
For each individual receipt document, SAP Business One also lets you assign a specific bin location to store the received items.
You can specify the bin location in the Bin Location field in the corresponding Form Settings window.
Once you assign a bin location to a receipt document using the form settings, this bin location will have priority over the
receiving bin locations or default bin locations mentioned in the following automatic allocation processes. On the other hand, if
you do not assign a bin location using the form settings, the following processes will take place in the receipt document as
described.
 Note
If you choose Save as Draft for documents where the receiving of items is involved, the following rules apply:
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 52

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
If you have not opened the Bin Location Allocation – Receipt window from the document, the results of automatic bin
location allocation will not be saved to the draft document; SAP Business One will perform the automatic bin location
allocation again next time you open this document, and display the allocation result in it
If you have opened the Bin Location Allocation – Receipt window from the document, and have successfully updated
the allocation result in this window, the updated allocation result will be saved to the draft document
Automatic Bin Location Allocation for Goods Received Externally
When you receive items purchased from your vendors or goods returned by your customers, SAP Business One can place these
items in different bin locations, depending on your warehouse structures, as follows:
Warehouse with Receiving Bin Locations
SAP Business One can automatically place the received items in the receiving bin locations of your warehouse. You can
then manually create an inventory transfer to move the items to the storage bin locations after conducting a quality check.
 Note
To facilitate the inventory transfer from receiving bin locations to storage bin locations, SAP Business One provides you
with the Clear Bin Locations function in the following two reports:
Bin Location List
Bin Location Content List
Automatic allocation of receiving bin locations takes place when the following conditions are met:
You have enabled receiving bin locations for your warehouse.
To do so, select the Enable Receiving Bin Locations checkbox on the Bin Locations tab of the Warehouses - Setup
window.
There are active empty receiving bin locations in your warehouse.
To indicate a bin location is a receiving bin location, in the Bin Location Master Data window, select the Receiving
Bin Location checkbox.
If you have enabled receiving bin locations for your warehouse but there is no active receiving bin location available, SAP
Business One does not perform the automatic bin location allocation. You must manually select the bin locations to which
you assign the received items.
When you have more than one receiving bin location in your warehouse, SAP Business One allocates the items to these bin
locations according to the order you specified in the Receive Items By field on the Bin Locations tab of the Warehouses -
Setup window.
If the quantity of items you receive exceeds the maximum storage limit of a receiving bin location, SAP Business One fills
this receiving bin location to the maximum and then assigns the remaining items to the next empty bin location in the
receiving bin location sequence.
 Note
Automatic allocation does not take place until you add the receipt document. Only then can the system accurately
check the availability and storage status of the receiving bin locations, and make sure the allocation in this document
does not conflict with any others.
If you have already manually allocated items to bin locations, either fully or partially, before adding the document, SAP
Business One does not reallocate these items to receiving bin locations.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 53

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
The following diagram shows the receipts of purchased or returned items to warehouses with receiving bin locations:
Warehouse Without Receiving Bin Locations
SAP Business One can automatically place the received items in the default bin locations if the following conditions are
met:
You have not enabled receiving bin locations for your warehouse.
You have specified a default bin location for the received item on the warehouse, item group or item level.
If you have specified bin locations on all three levels, the default bin location on the item level has the highest
priority. That is, SAP Business One places the received item in the default bin location you specified in the item
master data.
For more information, see Bin Locations.
The default bin location is active.
To indicate a bin location is active, leave the Inactive checkbox in the Bin Location Master Data window unselected.
 Note
If you have enforced the use of the default bin location for an item, the item must be allocated to the default bin location.
Even if you have specified a different bin location in the Form Settings window, SAP Business One still allocates the item
to the default bin location. In addition, you cannot manually allocate the item to any other bin locations.
When there is no active default bin location available, SAP Business One does not perform automatic bin location
allocation. You must manually select the bin locations to which you assign the received items.
If you have specified a maximum storage limit for the default bin location, the limit does not have any effect on the receipt
of items in this bin location. That is, even if the quantity of items you received exceeds the maximum limit, SAP Business
One still allocates these items to the default bin location.
 Note
Generally, automatic allocation takes place immediately after you specify the item, item quantity, and warehouse in the
receipt document row.
For serial and batch items under the management method On Every Transaction, automatic allocation takes place after
you specify the batch or serial information.

Automatic Bin Location Allocation for Goods Received Internally
When you receive items internally, for example, items transferred from one warehouse to another or finished products collected
from factories, SAP Business One can place these items directly in the default bin locations regardless of whether your warehouse
has receiving bin locations or not. Automatic allocation takes place when the following conditions are met:
You have specified a default bin location for the received item on the warehouse, item group, or item level.
If you have specified bin locations on all three levels, the default bin location on the item level has the highest priority. That
is, SAP Business One places the received item in the default bin location you specified in the item master data.
For more information, see Bin Locations.
The default bin location is active.
To indicate a bin location is active, leave the Inactive checkbox in the Bin Location Master Data window unselected.
 Note
If you have enforced the use of the default bin location, the item must be allocated to the default bin location. In this case, you
cannot manually allocate the item to any other bin locations.
When there is no active default bin location available, SAP Business One does not perform automatic bin location allocation. You
must manually select the bin locations to which you assign the received items.
If you have specified a maximum storage limit for the default bin location, the limit does not have any effect on the receipt of items
in this bin location. That is, even if the quantity of items you received exceeds the maximum limit, SAP Business One still allocates
these items to the default bin location.
 Note
Generally, automatic allocation takes place immediately after you specify the item, item quantity, and warehouse in the receipt
document row.
For serial and batch items under the management method On Every Transaction, automatic allocation takes place after you
specify the batch or serial information.

Context
During inventory receipts, while SAP Business One can allocate items to bin locations automatically, you can also perform the

The following procedure explains how to manually allocate items that are not managed by serials or batches to bin locations:
Procedure
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, open a receipt document.
For a list of all receipt documents, see Receipts to Bin Locations.
2. In the receipt document, specify the item, quantity and warehouse.

Different receipt documents let you open the window in several ways, as follows:
Inventory transfer

Items to Bin Locations.
All documents with the receiving of items, excluding inventory transfer
In the document, click to the left of the quantity in the Bin Location Allocation field in the row.
In the document, right-click in the row and choose Bin Location Allocation.
In the document, place your cursor in the row and press Ctrl + Shift + A .

Batch Allocation in Bin Locations Window
When you receive batch items that are managed on release only, you can allocate the items to the bin locations of your warehouse
without having to specify the batch information right away. Later, you can add the batch information for these items using batch
management, and link each batch to its corresponding bin locations using this window.
To access this window, proceed as follows:
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Item Management Batches Batch Management .
The Batch Management - Selection Criteria window opens.
2. In the Operation field, select Complete from the dropdown list.
3. Specify other selection criteria and choose OK.
The Batch Management - Complete window opens.
4. In the Rows from Documents table, select the row with the base receipt document for which you want to complete the
batch information.
5. In the Created Batches table, specify the batches and quantities. Then click in the Bin Location Allocation field.
