Automatic Allocation
To let SAP Business One allocate the items in bin locations to batches automatically, choose the pushbutton and select one of the
following options from the opened list:
Remaining – The system allocates the remaining quantity from the bin locations in the table if the remaining quantity is not
zero.
The system starts allocating the remaining quantity from the first bin location in the table. If the remaining quantity is
greater than the Total to Allocate quantity in the first bin location, the system allocates the rest from the second and the
following bin locations.
 Note
When you select any of the following five options, SAP Business One clears the current allocations and re-allocates the
item from bin locations according to the method you select.
Single Choice – The system allocates the item from bin locations using the single choice method.
Single choice is a method of allocating items from bin locations when there is only one way of doing so. If there is more than
one way to allocate the item, the single choice method is not effective.
For more information, see Automatic Bin Location Allocation in Issues.
Bin Location Code Order – The system allocates the item from bin locations according to the alphanumeric order of the
bin location codes.
Alternative Sort Code Order – The system allocates the item from bin locations according to the alphanumeric order of the
bin locations' alternative sort codes.
Descending Quantity – The system allocates the item from bin locations according to the descending order of the item
quantity in the bin locations.
Ascending Quantity – The system allocates the item from bin locations according to the ascending order of the item
quantity in the bin locations.
Ascending Quantity – Single Bin Preferred – The system allocates the item from a single bin location that fully satisfies
the required quantity. If more than one such bin location exists, the one with the least quantity is to be used.
If no single bin location satisfies the required quantity, the items are to be allocated from bin locations according to the
ascending order of the item quantity in the bin locations.

 Note
Typically, you use the above-listed documents or transactions to record the issuing of inventory. However, SAP Business One
also makes it possible for you to record the issuing of inventory using typical receipt documents, such as goods receipt PO or
A/P invoices. You can enter a negative quantity in these documents to indicate the issuing.
During the issuing of inventory, SAP Business One can pick the items from bin locations automatically, or you can manually
allocate the items from bin locations.

Automatic Bin Location Allocation in Issues
To facilitate bin location allocation during inventory issuing, SAP Business One enables you to automate the process of allocating
items from bin locations.
The automatic bin location allocation process can take place in all documents that involve the issuing of items. For a list of issue
documents, see Issues from Bin Locations.
During the issuing of inventory, SAP Business One can allocate items from bin locations automatically according to the following
methods:
Single Choice
The method of allocating items from bin locations when there is only one way of doing so. If there is more than one way to
allocate items from bin locations, the single choice method is not effective.
The single choice method is applicable only in the following situations:
The item you need to issue exists in only one bin location.
In this case, you must issue the item from this bin location.
The item you need to issue exists in more than one bin location and the entire inventory of the item must be used to
fulfill the requirement.
In this case, you must issue the entire inventory of the item from all the bin locations.
 Example
Example 1
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 73

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
You want to deliver item A with quantity 50 to a customer.
In your warehouse, you have 200 units of item A stored in bin location X.
In this case, even if your inventory greatly exceeds the committed quantity, you only allocate 50 from bin location X.
If single choice is the allocation method, SAP Business One automatically allocates the items from bin location X for the
delivery.
Example 2
You want to deliver item B with quantity 100 to a customer.
In your warehouse, you have exactly 100 units of item B stored as follows:
Bin location Y: 60
Bin location Z: 40
In this case, you can only pick 60 from bin location Y and 40 from bin location Z to fulfill the delivery.
If single choice is the allocation method, SAP Business One automatically allocates the items from the two bin locations
for the delivery.
Bin Location Code Order
The method of allocating items from bin locations according to the alphanumeric order of the bin location codes.
Alternative Sort Code Order
The method of allocating items from bin locations according to the alphanumeric order of the bin locations’ alternative sort
codes.
Descending Quantity
The method of allocating items from bin locations according to the descending order of the item quantity in the bin
locations.
Ascending Quantity
The method of allocating items from bin locations according to the ascending order of the item quantity in the bin
locations.
Ascending Quantity – Single Bin Preferred
The method of allocating items from a single bin location that fully satisfies the required quantity. If more than one such bin
location exists, the one with the least quantity is to be used.
If no single bin location satisfies the required quantity, the items are to be allocated from bin locations according to the
ascending order of the item quantity in the bin locations.
 Note
For a production order with components using a Backflush issue method, the components must be issued automatically from
the warehouses. For such components, SAP Business One automatically issues them from bin locations according to the
automatic allocation method you specified for the warehouse. If the allocation method is not effective, SAP Business One will
issue the components from their default bin locations. If the default bin locations do not exist, the system then takes the
components from the system bin locations.
SAP Business One lets you specify the bin location allocation method on the following levels:
Warehouse
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 74

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
On the warehouse level, you can specify a bin location allocation method which applies to all items issued from a
warehouse.
To do so, first open the Warehouses - Setup window and select the Bin Locations tab. Then, in the Auto Alloc. on Issue
field, select an allocation method.
Document
On the document level, you can specify a bin location allocation method which applies to all items in an issue document.
To do so, first open the Form Settings window from an issue document. Then, in the Automatic Allocation field, select an
allocation method.
Document Row
On the document row level, you can specify a bin location allocation method which only applies to the item in a particular
row of an issue document. To do so, there are different ways for different kinds of items, as follows:
Items Not Managed by Serials or Batches
If the item in the document row is not managed by serials or batches, you can appoint an allocation method for the
item in the Bin Location Allocation - Issue window. In this window, choose the Automatic Allocation pushbutton
and select a method from the opened list.
For more information about how to open the window from a row of an issue document, see Bin Location Allocation -
Issue Window.
Items Managed by Serials
If the item in the document row is a serial item and is issued primarily by bin locations, you can appoint an allocation
method for the item in the Serial Number Selection window. In this window, choose the Selection Method
pushbutton and select a method from the opened list.
For more information about how to open the window from a row of an issue document, see Serial Number Selection
Window.
If the item in the document row is a serial item and is issued primarily by serial numbers, the system does not
perform the automatic bin location allocation. Instead, you can select the items you want to issue by their serial
numbers, and then these items are directly taken from the bin locations where they are stored.
Items Managed by Batches
If the item in the document row is a batch item and is issued primarily by bin locations, you can appoint an allocation
method for the item in the Batch Number Selection window. In this window, choose the Selection Method
pushbutton and select a method from the opened list.
If the item in the document row is a batch item and is issued primarily by batch numbers, you must first select the
batches that you want to issue, and then the system can allocate these batch items automatically from bin
locations. In this case, you can appoint an allocation method by choosing the Automatic Allocation pushbutton in
the Batch Number Selection window.
For more information about how to open the window from a row of an issue document, see Batch Number Selection
Window.
 Note
If you choose Save as Draft for documents where the issuing of items is involved, the following rules apply:
If you have not opened the Bin Location Allocation – Issue window from the document, the results of automatic bin
location allocation will not be saved to the draft document; SAP Business One will perform the automatic bin location
allocation again next time you open this document, and display the allocation result in it

• If you have opened the Bin Location Allocation – Issue window from the document, and have successfully updated
the allocation result in this window, the updated allocation result will be saved to the draft document

Allocating Regular Items from Bin Locations
Prerequisites
You have enabled bin locations for your warehouse.
For more information, see Enabling Bin Locations.
Context
During the issuing of inventory, while SAP Business One can allocate items from bin locations automatically, you can also perform
the allocation manually.
For more information about the automatic allocation, see Automatic Bin Location Allocation in Issues.
The following procedure explains how to manually allocate items that are not managed by serials or batches from bin locations.
Procedure
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, open an issue document.
For a list of issue documents, see Issues from Bin Locations.
2. In the issue document, specify the item, quantity and warehouse.
3. Open the Bin Location Allocation - Issue window in the row for which you want to perform the bin location allocation.
Different issue documents let you open the window in several ways, as follows:
Inventory transfer
In the Inventory Transfer window, click to the left of the quantity in the From Bin Locations field in the
row.
In the Inventory Transfer window, right-click in the row and choose Allocate Items from Bin Locations.
In the Inventory Transfer window, place your cursor in the row and from the Go To menu, choose Allocate
Items from Bin Locations.
All documents with the issuing of items, excluding inventory transfer
In the document, click to the left of the quantity in the Bin Location Allocation field in the row.
In the document, right-click in the row and choose Bin Location Allocation.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 76

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
In the document, place your cursor in the row and press Ctrl + Shift + A .
In the document, place your cursor in the row and from the Go To menu, choose Bin Location Allocation.
4. In the Bin Location Allocation - Issue window, select the bin locations from which you want to issue the items and specify
how many of each item you want to issue from each bin location.
 Note
SAP Business One lets you allocate an item from a bin location even if the allocation causes the inventory of the item in
the bin location to fall below zero. This makes it possible for you to record an issue document in advance when your
inventory falls short of the requirement of the issue document.
To allow negative inventory of an item, select the Allow Negative Inventory checkbox in the corresponding row.
If SAP Business One has already allocated the item from bin locations, you can first clear the allocations by choosing the
Clear Allocations pushbutton.
 Note
You must fully allocate the item from bin locations till the Remaining quantity is zero. Otherwise, you cannot add the
issue document.
5. In the Bin Location Allocation - Issue window, choose OK. The window closes.
6. To add the issue document, choose Add in the document.

Allocating Serial or Batch Items from Bin Locations
Prerequisites
You have enabled bin locations for your warehouse.
For more information, see Enabling Bin Locations.
You have specified whether you want to pick the serial and batch items according to their bin locations or serial and batch
information.
To indicate your preference for a serial or batch item, proceed as follows:
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Item Master Data .
2. On the General tab of the Item Master Data window, in the Manage Item by field, specify whether you want to
manage the item by serials or batches.
3. In the Issue Primarily By field, select how you pick the item for issuing, by either of the following:
Serial and Batch Numbers – Picks the item you want to issue by its serial or batch information.
A serial item can exist in only one bin location. Therefore, selecting the serial number automatically selects
its associated bin location.
A batch of items can exist in various bin locations. After you specify which batch and how many items in the
batch you want to issue, you must specify from which bin locations these batch items are going to be issued.
Bin Locations – Picks the item you want to issue by its bin locations.
A serial item can exist in only one bin location. Therefore, selecting the bin location automatically selects its
serial number.
A batch of items can exist in various bin locations. And each bin location can contain various batches. SAP
Business One makes a list of all bin locations that contain the item and presents in detail which batch and
how many of the batch items are in each bin location.
 Note
In order for you to pick items according to the two criteria, SAP Business One provides you with two different
layouts in the Serial Number Selection and Batch Number Selection windows.
Context
During inventory issue, while SAP Business One can allocate serial and batch items from bin locations automatically, you can also
allocate manually.
For more information about the automatic allocation, see Automatic Bin Location Allocation in Issues.
The following procedure explains how to manually allocate serial and batch items from bin locations.
Procedure
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 80

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, open an issue document.
2. In the issue document, specify the serial or batch item, quantity and warehouse.
3. Open the Serial Numbers - Setup or the Batches - Setup window.
To do so, place the cursor in the Quantity field of the issue document and proceed accordingly:
Inventory transfer
Right-click and choose Allocate Serials/Batches from Whse.
From the Go To menu, choose Allocate Serials/Batches from Whse.
All documents with the issuing of items, excluding inventory transfer
For a list of issue documents, see Issues from Bin Locations.
Press Ctrl + Tab .
Right-click and choose Batch/Serial Numbers.
From the Go To menu, choose Batch/Serial Numbers.
4. To select the serials or batches from bin locations, proceed in one of the following ways:
Serial Items – Issued Primarily by Serial Numbers
In the Serial Number Selection window, select the serial numbers that you want to issue in the Available Serial
Numbers table, and move them to the Selected Serial Numbers table.
Serial Items – Issued Primarily by Bin Locations
In the Serial Number Selection window, in the Available Serial Numbers table, select the bin locations from which
you want to issue the serial items, and move them to the Selected Serial Numbers table.
To move the serial items automatically from the Available Serial Numbers table to the Selected Serial Numbers
table, choose the Selection Method pushbutton and select the automatic allocation method from the opened list.
Batch Items – Issued Primarily by Batch Numbers
In the Batch Number Selection window, select the batches you want to issue from the Available Batches table to
the Selected Batches table. Then, in the Selected Batches table, specify from which bin locations you want to issue
the selected batches using the Bin Location Allocation field.

Serial Number Selection Window
Use this window to automatically enter or update numerous serial numbers for the item in one step.
The window is opened for the following transactions:
Inventory issue transactions: The window opens automatically when you choose the Add button on the document window.
Alternatively, to open the Serial Number Selection window, place the cursor in the Quantity field and do one of the
following to open the window:
Press CTRL + TAB .
Right-click and choose Batch/Serial Numbers.
From the Go To menu, choose Batch/Serial Numbers.
Inventory counting transactions: You do not have to enter serial numbers for inventory counting documents, but they are
mandatory for inventory posting transactions. For inventory counting documents, this window is named as Serial Number
Counting; for inventory posting documents, this window is named as Serial Number Posting.
You can select only those rows that contain items with serial numbers.
In the Serial Number Selection window, the Rows From Documents table displays the list of the serial number-managed item
rows from the relevant documents.

information.
General Notes
To open the Serial Number Details window, click to the left of the serial number.
If not all the required serial numbers are selected, the Serial Number Selection window opens again while you are adding
the document.
You can add and update serial numbers in this window as long as the document is not added to the system and no
inventory transaction is posted.
In the Serial Number Selection window, from the Go To menu, choose Serial Numbers Completion, or right-click in the
window and choose the same option. The Serial Numbers Management - Selection Criteria window opens in Complete
mode for that specific item. For more information, see Serial Number Management - Update/Complete Window.
Copying Documents - If you selected serial numbers in a base document that created an inventory transaction, and you
copied this document to a target document, you will not be able to view the serial numbers data in the target document,
unless the document is one of the following: return, A/R credit memo, goods return, or A/P credit memo.
When generating an A/R reserve invoice, you cannot select serial numbers for release, since the reserve invoice does not
create an inventory release transaction.
Inventory Transfer - When generating an inventory transfer document, the following apply:
For serial number items that are managed on every transaction, select which serial numbers to transfer from the
source warehouse by pressing CTRL + TAB while pointing at the Quantity field.
For serial number items that are managed on release only, there is no need to define which serial numbers will enter
the target warehouse. The transaction is automatically performed between the two warehouses.

Automatic Allocation
Select the method by which items are automatically allocated from bin locations during issue. You can select one of the following
methods:
Single Choice – Allocates items from bin locations when there is only one way of doing it. If there is more than one way to
allocate items from bin locations, the single choice method is not effective.
The single choice method is applicable only in one of the following situations:
The item you need to issue exists only in one bin location.
In this case, there is no other way of issuing the item but from this bin location.
The item you need to issue exists in more than one bin location and the entire inventory of the item must be taken to
fulfill the requirement.
In this case, there is no other way of issuing the entire inventory of the item but from all the bin locations.
 Example
For more information, see the Auto Alloc. on Issue field in Warehouses - Setup: Bin Locations Tab.
Bin Location Code Order – Allocates items from bin locations according to the alphanumeric order of the bin location
codes
Alternative Sort Code Order – Allocates items from bin locations according to the alphanumeric order of the bin locations'
alternative sort codes
Descending Quantity – Allocates items from bin locations according to the descending order of the item quantity in the bin
locations
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 86

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
Ascending Quantity – Allocates items from bin locations according to the ascending order of the item quantity in the bin
locations
Ascending Quantity – Single Bin Preferred – Allocates items from a single bin location that fully satisfies the required
quantity. If more than one such bin location exists, the one with the least quantity is to be used.
If no single bin location satisfies the required quantity, the items are to be allocated from bin locations according to the
ascending order of the item quantity in the bin locations.
FIFO - Allocates items from bin locations according to the "First In, First Out" principle
LIFO - Allocates items from bin locations according to the "Last In, First Out" principle

Batch Number Selection Window
Use this window to add and update batches for documents.
When you add a new batch that already exists in another warehouse, a warning message appears. If you select the OK button, the
attributes of the newly entered batch are overwritten by the attributes of the existing batch, including user-defined fields.
When the same batch already exists in the customer's system, in more than one warehouse with a different attribute, when you try
to add a new batch with the same batch number, the attributes of the newly entered batch are overwritten by the attributes from
the batch that was created first. But if more than one entry exists for the same batch on the same creation date, then the
attributes of the newly created batch are overwritten randomly by one of those batches.
If the existing batch has no attributes at all, batches created afterwards will have no attributes as well.
The Location attribute is not overwritten by the location from an existing batch. It retains its setting in the Batches - Setup window
(or empty if you did not enter any value).
For more information about accessing this window, see Defining and Selecting Batches on Release Only.

with a negative quantity, and A/R credit memo.

Bin Locations in Pick and Pack
With bin locations enabled for the warehouses in your company, the identification of specific bin locations to pick from becomes a
key element of the pick and pack process.
SAP Business One makes it possible for you to allocate items from bin locations throughout the entire pick and pack process. The
allocation can be automatic, but you can also manually assign the bin locations.
In addition, to facilitate the picking process, you can create pick lists for specific warehouses, warehouse sublevels, and bin
locations.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 94

Pick List Generation Wizard
Creating Multiple Pick Lists
Prerequisites
You have enabled bin locations for your warehouse.
For more information, see Enabling Bin Locations.
Context
With the Pick List Generation Wizard in pick and pack, you can create multiple pick lists for the following selected document rows:
Sales order
A/R reserve invoice
Production order
Inventory transfer request
While creating pick lists using the pick list generation wizard, you can split the pick lists by the following:
Warehouse
Warehouse sublevels
Bin location attributes
By splitting pick lists, you can facilitate the picking process and greatly improve the picking efficiency. For instance, in the below
example, if you split pick lists by warehouse, two pick lists are generated. You can send two pickers, one to each warehouse to
collect the items for delivery.
Procedure
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Pick and Pack Pick and Pack Manager .
2. In the Pick and Pack Manager - Selection Criteria window, specify the selection criteria and choose OK.
3. In the Pick and Pack Manager – Open Drawer, select the sales order, A/R reserve invoice, production order, and inventory
transfer request rows for which you want to create the pick lists, enter the quantity you want to release to the pick lists, and
choose the Released to Pick List pushbutton.

Example
You company has two warehouses – warehouse A and warehouse B.
The two warehouses have the same following structure:
Warehouse Sublevel 1 – Wing

Warehouse Sublevel 2 – Section
Sublevel codes – SECTIONA and SECTIONB, which represent section A and B in each wing.
Warehouse Sublevel 3 – Shelf
Sublevel codes – SHELF01 and SHELF02, which stand for shelf 01 and 02 in each section.

Allocating Regular Items from Bin Locations in Pick and Pack
Prerequisites
You have enabled bin locations for at least one warehouse in your company.
For more information, see Enabling Bin Locations.
The items you commit in the sales order, A/R reserve invoice, production order, and inventory transfer request document
rows are stored in warehouses with bin locations.
The items you commit in the sales order, A/R reserve invoice, production order, and inventory transfer request document
rows are not managed by serials or batches.
Context
SAP Business One lets you allocate items from bin locations throughout the entire pick and pack process.
To allocate items that are not managed by serials or batches from bin locations in pick and pack, proceed as follows:
Procedure
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Pick and Pack Pick and Pack Manager .
2. In the Pick and Pack Manager - Selection Criteria window, specify the selection criteria and choose OK.
3. In the Pick and Pack Manager - Open Drawer, select the sales order, A/R reserve invoice, production order, and inventory
transfer request rows for which you want to create pick lists, enter the quantity you want to release to the pick lists, and
choose the Release to Pick List pushbutton.
The Pick List Generation Wizard opens.
4. In step 1 of the wizard, select a range of bin locations from which you want to allocate the items by specifying the
warehouse sublevels and bin location attributes.
5. In step 2 of the wizard, select the method by which the items in the pick lists are automatically allocated from bin locations.
6. In step 3 of the wizard, specify the general information about the pick lists and choose the Generate pushbutton.
The pick lists are generated with the items allocated from bin locations according to the range and method you specified in
step 4 and 5, respectively.
7. To manually change the bin location allocation, open the Bin Location Allocation - Issue window by doing either of the
following in the Pick and Pack Manager - Released Drawer:
Click to the left of the quantity in the Bin Location Allocation field.
Right-click in the pick list row and choose Bin Location Allocation.
Place your cursor in the pick list row and press Ctrl + Shift + A .
Place your cursor in the row and from the Go To menu, choose Bin Location Allocation.
8. To manually change the bin location allocation again while picking the items for delivery, open the Bin Location Allocation -
Issue window by doing either of the following in the Pick List window:
Right-click in the pick list row and choose Bin Location Allocation.
Place your cursor in the pick list row and press Ctrl + Shift + A .
Place your cursor in the row and from the Go To menu, choose Bin Location Allocation.
Related Information
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 98

warehouse for them.
These document rows are not included in the same pick list as those which have warehouses with bin locations enabled.
Automatic Allocation
Select the method by which the items in the pick lists are automatically allocated from the bin locations you selected in the first
step of the wizard.
You can select from among the following:
Bin Location Code Order – Allocates items from bin locations according to the alphanumeric order of the bin location
codes
Alternative Sort Code Order – Allocates items from bin locations according to the alphanumeric order of the bin locations’
alternative sort codes
Descending Quantity – Allocates items from bin locations according to the descending order of the item quantity in the bin
locations
Ascending Quantity – Allocates items from bin locations according to the ascending order of the item quantity in the bin
locations
Ascending Quantity – Single Bin Preferred – Allocates items from a single bin location that fully satisfies the required
quantity. If more than one such bin location exists, the one with the least quantity is to be used.
If no single bin location satisfies the required quantity, the items are to be allocated from bin locations according to the
ascending order of the item quantity in the bin locations.
FIFO - Allocates items from bin locations according to the "First In, First Out" principle
LIFO - Allocates items from bin locations according to the "Last In, First Out" principle
Warehouse Settings - Allocates items by the same method as defined for Auto Alloc. on Issue in the Warehouses - Setup
window
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 103

Price Lists
SAP Business One lets you create different price lists for items, giving you the flexibility to offer your customers customized prices.
During the creation of sales and purchasing documents, SAP Business One derives item prices directly from a price list that is
linked to a business partner. This price list can be linked by default from the business partner's group or from the business
partner's payment terms, or can be selected manually in the business partner master data. When you add a business transaction
for a business partner, the price of the item is determined by the assigned price list.
When you initialize SAP Business One, you define data for business partners, business partner groups, and payment terms, as well
as the price lists for customers and vendors. This data is revised and modified over the course of time, resulting in price
information used in sales and purchasing that is always up to date.
SAP Business One provides 10 default price lists. You can use from any to all 10 of them. You can define new price lists and delete
existing ones. You can also link different price lists to one another using multiplication factors. In each price list you can define up
to three prices with different currencies for each item. In addition, you can set different prices for each of the item's units of
measurement (UoM). Maintaining different price lists for items makes it possible to set special prices and quantity-dependent
discounts in each one, thereby letting you offer your customers customized prices.
You can choose for items with no price to be removed from the database level by selecting the Remove Unpriced Items from price
list Database checkbox in General Settings. For more information about this setting, see General Settings: Pricing Tab.
In SAP Business One, you define prices for items in price lists. A price list can be assigned to a business partner through his
business partner group or his payment terms.

 Note

You can choose the following rules for rounding:
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 119

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
Round to Closest
Round Up
Round Down
Round to Closest is chosen by default.
Ending/Interval
Enables you to define fixed rounded amounts to the digits.
 Note
This column is available and only mandatory for the Fixed Ending and Fixed Interval rounding methods.
There are 3 boxes in this column, for example x x x . x x . The character x is a placeholder and can be changed to any other
digits between 0 to 9. The first 3 boxes are for the definition of the fixed full amount and the other 2 boxes are for the definition of
the fixed decimal amount. The number of boxes for the decimal amount and the separator sign can be changed under
Administration General Settings Display .
Each of the boxes represents the fixed value of the related place in the price. For example, xxx.x9 represents 9 cents, while xx9.xx
represents 9 dollars.
For the fixed ending method, xxx.x9 means that the last decimal digit is 9 and offers the following rounding options: 100.19, 150.29,
50.99, and so on.
For the fixed interval method, xxx.25 means that the original value and the rounded value are 0.25 different from each other, and it
offers the following rounding options: 100.25, 100.50, 100.75, 101.00, and so on.
After defining the ending/interval value, you can choose Copy to Field to save your changes as a string. For a fixed ending, if you
define the value as xx9.xx and leave the decimal part empty, after saving, the value is converted to xx9.00. For a fixed interval, if
you define the value as xx9.xx, after saving, the value is converted to 009.00.
In the case of negative prices, the rounding is performed according to the correct mathematical calculation.
The definition of rounding methods and rules is associated with the price list, therefore, all items and currencies under the same
price list have the same rounding definition.
Authorization Group
The authorization group is used to control access to a price list and is defined under the subject Inventory Price Lists Price
Lists in the Authorizations window.
 Example
You have defined three price lists PL01, PL02 and PL03 and want to give a specific group of users full access to PL01, read only
access to PL02 and no access to PL03. In this case, proceed as follows:
1. In the Price List window, do the following:
If you're running SAP Business One 9.3 PL08 or earlier, select Group 1 for PL01, Group 2 for PL02, and Group 3
for PL03.
If you're running SAP Business One 9.3 PL09 or later, select Price List - Group No. 1 for PL01, Price List - Group
No. 2 for PL02, and Price List - Group No. 3 for PL03.
2. In the User Groups window, create a new user group named <Group A> and select Authorization for the Group Type.
3. On the Groups tab in the Authorizations window, select Group A.

This window displays an item's prices in a specific price list. It is possible to define up to three prices with different currencies
(Primary Currency, Additional Currency 1 and Additional Currency 2) for each item in each price list. This functionality can be
used to define an exact additional price without the original price being converted to a different currency during document
processing.
 Note
By default, the Primary Currency - Unit Price is taken into the Unit Price field in a document, unless the document's currency
matches one of the additional currencies, and then the relevant additional currency price is taken.

Price List Creation
Entering various price lists into SAP Business One lets you create pricing recommendations. These are appropriate for pricing
items in particular transactions.
SAP Business One provides ten predefined price lists. Adding, changing, or deleting these prices enables you to map a pricing
tactic in SAP Business One. Using all or a few of the defined price lists is optional.
Furthermore, the following two price lists are automatically created and calculated by SAP Business One and cannot be manually
changed:
Last Purchase Price
This price list is automatically updated when an item enters the inventory with an original price.
Last Evaluated Price
This price list is automatically updated after you run the Inventory Valuation simulation report or the Inventory Audit report.
 Note
The Inventory Valuation report is available to companies managing non perpetual inventory.
The Last Evaluated Price is calculated only for an item's inventory UoM, and only in the primary currency.
In order for the Inventory Audit report to update the last evaluated price, the following conditions must be met:
The item is not managed by the serial/batch valuation method.
On the Basic Initialization tab in the Company Details window, the Manage Item Cost per Warehouse checkbox
is selected.
If the checkbox is deselected, the calculation of the Last Evaluated Price will be based on transactions for all
warehouses.
The default warehouse is specified for the item in the Item Master Data window or on the Items subtab of the
Inventory tab in the General Settings window.
When running the Inventory Audit Report, calculation of the item cost from the default warehouse will update the
Last Evaluated Price. SAP Business One first checks the default warehouse for the item specified in the Item
Master Data window; if it does not exist, then the company default warehouse from the General Settings
window is used. If there are no transactions for the item involving its default warehouse or the company's default
warehouse, then the Last Evaluated Price will not be updated. For items valuated by the FIFO method, the next
price layer to be issued will be used.
Process
1. Define one or more base price lists in which you enter the price of each item. You then refer all the other price lists you
define to the base price list, with a particular factor. The advantage of this is that you enter prices once and SAP Business
One automatically calculates the valid prices for particular cases according to the base price list.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 131

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
 Example
Creating price list A for regular customers, and price list B for customers who make occasional purchases. The prices in
price list B are to be 10% higher. When defining price list B, refer it to price list A with a factor of 1.1. SAP Business One
then chooses the higher price for the occasional customer, whose master data record is assigned price list B.
2. Adjusting all prices is possible by changing them once in the base price list. The changes are made automatically in all price
lists that refer to the base price list.
3. Changing the ratio between two price lists is possible by, changing the factor once. Considering the previous example, the
factor is changed to 1.15, setting the prices for occasional customers 15% higher than those for regular customers.

enter the required factor.
Updating a New Base (Independent) Price List

Updating Price Lists
In SAP Business One you can update price lists by any of the following methods:
Updating entire price lists
Updating prices by selection
Updating prices manually
These methods are described in the sections below.
 Note
When you update a price list that is a base price list for other price lists, the prices in those lists change accordingly. In the case
of an independent price list, the factor reverts to 1 after you update.
Updating Entire Price Lists
Procedure
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Price Lists Price Lists .
2. In the Price Lists window, in the upper left area, select the Update Entire Price List radio button.
3. In the row of the price list you want to update, change any of the following:
In the Price List Name column, enter a name.
In the Base Price List column, in the dropdown list, select a price list.
In the Factor column, enter the factor by which the base price list is multiplied to calculate the prices in the selected
price list.
In the Rounding Method column, in the dropdown list, select a rounding method.
In the Authorization Group column, in the dropdown list, select an authorization group.
In the Active column, select whether the price list is active or inactive.
In the Valid From and Valid To columns, enter a date range to determine a validity period for the price list
4. Choose the Update button.
5. Double-click the row of the price list whose entire list of items you want to update.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 133

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
6. In the [Price Lists Name] Window, in the Unit Price column of any one of the currencies, make the required changes, and
choose the Update button.
7. Double-click the row of an item with an Inventory UoM other than Manual, that you want to update.
8. In the [Price List Name] – UoM Prices window, in the Unit Price and the Reduced By % columns of any one of the
currencies, make the required changes for any of the units of measurement and choose the Update button.
 Note
If you have updated an independent price list, in the Price Lists window, in the row of the new price list, in the Factor
column, the factor again appears as 1, since the price list is based on itself.
9. Choose the OK button.
Updating Prices by Selection
Procedure
In this procedure, you update only the item prices in the selected range. Other item prices do not change.
 Example
The Peaches and Cream fruit store divides its price lists according to seasonal fruit. The Berries price list requires updating in
the winter, when fruit is out of season and the prices must reflect the higher import costs. Annie, the owner, updates the factor
from 1 to 1.5.
She selects Update By Selection and chooses the Update button. When the Price List - Selection Criteria window opens, she
selects the Berries item group. The new factor applies only to the items belonging to this group. After she chooses the OK
button, the berry prices are updated for the selected items and groups only.
 Note
When you update the prices of the selected item range, the prices of these items are updated automatically in price lists linked
to the current price list.
 Note
In the Factor column, the factor displayed is the one defined during the last update.
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Price Lists Price Lists .
2. In the Price Lists window, in the upper left area, select the Update by Selection radio button.
3. In the row of the price list you want to update, change any of the following:
In the Price List Name column, enter a name.
In the Factor column, enter the factor by which the base price list is multiplied to calculate the prices in the selected
price list.
In the Authorization Group column, in the dropdown list, select an authorization group.
In the Active column, select whether the price list is active or inactive.
In the Valid From and Valid To columns, enter a date range to determine a validity period for the price list

4. Choose the Update button.

Linking Price Lists
Context
SAP Business One allows you to link price lists to one another by defining multiplication factors. You can enter the item prices in
only one price list, link it to other price lists using a certain factor and leave SAP Business One to calculate the prices automatically
in each one of the linked price lists.
 Caution
Back-up the database before making any global changes to the price lists.
Procedure
1. From the Main Menu choose Inventory Price Lists Price Lists .
The Price Lists window opens.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 136

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
2. In the Base Price List column, select the required base price list.
3. In the Factor column, enter the factor according to which you want to multiply the prices of the base price list (Base Price *
Factor = Price).
4. In the Rounding Method column, select the required rounding method from the dropdown list. This rounding method is
used for calculating the price according to the factor.
5. Choose Update to save your changes.
6. To view the new item prices, double-click the price list row number.
Results
The prices in the price list are calculated automatically according to the base price list, the multiplication factor, and the rounding
method.

Price Lists: Last Evaluated Price
To create the Last Evaluated Price price list, SAP Business One uses the last calculated cost for each item. If you run a valuation
under the FIFO method, for example, and then run a valuation for the last calculated costs, SAP Business One valuates the items
using the last value that was determined for an item under the FIFO method.
 Note
Last evaluated price is calculated only for the item's inventory UoM (displayed on the Inventory Data tab in the Item Master
Data record), and only in primary currency. No last evaluated price is calculated for any other UoMs that may have been
defined for the item.
 Note
You cannot change the Last Evaluated Price price list manually.
More Information
Price List Creation
Price Lists: Last Purchase Price
The prices in the Last Purchase Price price list are updated automatically when you perform any of the following tasks:
Entering an A/P invoice or A/P reserve invoice
 Note
If the invoice contains freight charges, and if the Last Purchase Price checkbox in the settings windows of the freights is
selected, then the freights affect the last purchase prices. In a perpetual inventory system, however, the last purchase
prices of drop-ship items (items that are received into drop-ship warehouses) and non-inventory items are not affected
by freights. For more information, see Managing Freight Charges.
If the invoice is based on a goods receipt PO (GRPO) for which you have recorded landed costs, the A/P invoice does not
update the last purchase prices of items that are included in the landed costs document.
Cancellation of the invoice does not affect last purchase prices, that is, adding a cancellation document neither updates
nor reverts the Last Purchase Price list. For more information, see Canceling Sales and Purchasing Documents.
Entering a goods receipt
Entering a positive opening balance for an item
Entering a positive inventory taking result (inventory posting) that triggers a goods receipt
Entering a landed costs document
 Note
If you have recorded landed costs for a GRPO, recording landed costs for an A/P invoice based on the GRPO updates
last purchase prices only for items that are NOT included in the existing landed costs document.
Entering a receipt from production based on standard or special production orders:
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 140

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
FIFO or MAP product in a perpetual inventory system: Its last purchase price is updated with the sum of the product
components' item costs.
Standard-priced product in a non-perpetual inventory system: Its last purchase price is updated with the product's
predefined item cost (displayed as the unit price in the receipt from production). If you does not define a cost for the
BOM item, its last purchase price is never updated.
Product in a non-perpetual inventory system: Its last purchase price is updated with the product's unit price defined
in the receipt from production.
If none of the above transactions occurs, an item's last purchase price is not updated
 Note
When you post one of the documents mentioned above using a date prior to the last update date of a certain item, the item's
last purchase price is not updated.
Zero prices never update the Last Purchase Price price list even if freight charges or landed costs exist.
 Note
Last purchase price is calculated for the UoMs that are used in the transactions only. Prices of other UoMs are not to be
calculated according to the conversion rule defined in the UoM group. For more information about the item UoM prices, see
[Price Lists Name] - UoM Prices Window
You cannot change the prices in the Last Purchase Price price list manually. That is, as long as an item has not been entered into
the warehouse in one of the ways mentioned above, it will not have a last purchase price.
The last purchase price can be used as a base price for other price lists. You can refer other price lists to the Last Purchase Price
price list using a defined factor.

Period and Volume Discounts
Use this function if you want special prices to depend on the items and associated price lists, and not directly on the business
partners.
If a customer purchases an item, and neither a special price nor a discount group has been defined for the customer or this item,
the special prices for the price list apply. This is the price list specified in the business partner master record.
 Example
The Watering Can in Garden Price List 8 has a price of $30. However, the price of oil has risen and the manager decides to raise
the whole price list by a factor of 1.5 to reflect the higher costs of transporting the inventory to her remote store. The updated
price for the Watering Can is now $45.
In reviewing the updated price list, the manager decides that the new prices are quite high for some items. Since she wants to
increase sales over the summer, she offers a discount, just for the Watering Can, during July and August, by entering 20 in the
Discount column, signifying a reduction of 20%. The price after discount is $36.
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 141

displayed in blue, which indicates that a discounted price is applied in certain conditions.

Managing Period and Volume Discounts
The procedures below describe how to manage special prices in price lists.
Procedure
Defining Date-Dependent Special Prices for a Price List
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Price Lists Period and Volume Discounts .
2. In the Period and Volume Discounts window, in the Price List dropdown list, select the price list for which you want to
define special prices.
3. To specify the item or items, do one of the following:
Choose the Add Items button.
The Special Prices – Items – Selection Criteria Window appears. You can use this window to copy a range of
selected items in one step.
Place your cursor in the Item No. column and click the Tab button. In the List of Items window, you can select
items to add.
In the Item No. column, enter the number of the item you want to add.
 Note
After you enter an item number, SAP Business One automatically displays the appropriate item description. The usual
search functions are available to help you find an item in SAP Business One.
4. In the Source Price column, select one of the price currencies.
5. To edit the date-dependent special prices, double-click the row number of the required item.
The Period Discounts Window appears.
6. To confirm your entries, choose the Update button.

Discount Groups
You can define more general discounts, that is, discount groups. You can define four different types of discount groups as follows:
For all Business Partners
For a specific customer group
For a specific vendor group
For a specific business partner
In each of the above discount groups' types, you can define any of the following discount groups:
Item group discount
A combination of item properties discount
Item manufacturer discount
Item specific discount
This discount is applied to the price list specified for the business partner in the master record.
Multiple discounts can be defined in any discount groups. For example, if you have defined a discount group for Item groups, you
can define in the same discount groups also discounts for manufacturers. Then, in the Business Partner Master Data record or in
the Business Partner group definition, you can define the ratio between the different discounts for the effective discount
calculation.
In each discount group you can set discount percentage or you can define variable discount according to the bought quantity. You
can also set any defined discount group as active or inactive.
To define discount groups, choose Inventory Price Lists Special Prices Discount Groups .
The discount groups are defined on the following tabs:
Item Groups
Properties
Manufacturers
Items

Copying Discount Groups

next to the group name.

The following discount group is defined for a particular item group, based on "buy 3, get 1 free":
| Group        | Paid Qty | Free Qty | Max. Free Qty |     |
| ------------ | -------- | -------- | ------------- | --- |
| Item Group 1 | 2        | 1        | 4             |     |

| 2        |     | 0             | Unit Price * 2 | No discount               |
| 3        |     | 33.33         | Unit Price * 2 | Pay for 2 and get 1 free  |
| 4        |     | 25            | Unit Price * 3 | Pay for 3 and get 1 free  |
| 5        |     | 20            | Unit Price * 4 | Pay for 4 and get 1 free  |
| 6        |     | 33.33         | Unit Price * 4 | Pay for 4 and get 2 free  |
| 12       |     | 33.33         | Unit Price * 8 | Pay for 8 and get 4 free  |
| 15       |     | 26.67         | Unit Price * 9 | Pay for 11 and get only 4 |
free, since this is the
maximum allowed as
defined

Disc. Relations:
Use when there are discounts for more than one property. Select one of the following options from the list:
Lowest: The property with the lowest discount determines the overall discount calculated for the item.
Highest: The property with the highest discount determines the overall discount calculated for the item.
Average: The system calculates the average of all the discounts for the properties. The average is used as the discount.
Total: The system adds together all discounts of the properties that apply to the item. The total (up to 100%) is used as the
discount.
Multiplied: The system multiplies all discounts of the properties that apply to the item. The result is used as the discount.

Special Prices
SAP Business One lets you define special prices for your customers and vendors in addition to the standard price lists. You can
define these special prices for specific business partners or by discount groups according to item groups, properties,
manufacturers, or items.
You can define special prices only in one currency, based on one of the item's prices (each item can have up to three unit prices
with different currencies). In addition, you can set different special prices for each unit of measurement (UoM) of the item.
When you process a sales or purchasing document, SAP Business One checks the following elements to determine the item prices
in the document:
Are there special prices defined for the business partner?
Are there discount groups linked to the business partner?
Are there period and volume discounts defined for the price list that is linked to the business partner?
Which price list is linked to the partner?

Defining Special Prices for Business Partners
Use the procedures below to define the following types of special prices for business partners:
Date-dependent
Quantity-based
Procedure
Defining Date-Dependent Special Prices for a Business Partner
You can define date-dependent special prices for particular periods. If an item is sold within one of these periods, the date-
dependent special price applies, ignoring the price in the price list.
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Price Lists Special Prices Special Prices for Business
Partners .
The Special Prices for Business Partners window appears.
2. To define the special price of an item for a business partner, in the Special Prices for Business Partners window, enter the
required business partner and item information.
3. In the Source Price column, select one of the price's currencies. The default is Unit Price – Primary Currency.
 Note
You can define special prices only in one currency, based on the selected item's price currency.
You must choose a source price which has a value for the specific item, in the specific price list, to be able to
base the special price on that price.
The Source Price column is disabled when you choose any of the following options in the Price List field:
Without Price List, Last Purchase Price, or Last Evaluated Price. For those options, only the primary currency
price is relevant.
4. To open the Period Discounts window, in the # column, double-click a row. Enter the required dates, price list, discount, and
price after discount and choose the Update button.
 Note
If no date-dependent special price has been defined for an item, SAP Business One assumes that the customer-specific
special price has been valid since the date on which it was added. The special price with the appropriate valid-from date
appears in the first row.
5. To save the modified special prices, in the Special Prices for Business Partners window, choose the Update button.
Defining Quantity-Based Special Prices for a Business Partner
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 157

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
1. From the SAP Business One Main Menu, choose Inventory Price Lists Special Prices Special Prices for Business
Partners .
The Special Prices for Business Partners window appears.
2. To open the Period Discounts window, in the # column, double-click a row. Enter the required dates, price list, discount, and
price after discount.
3. In the Period Discounts window, double-click a price-list row to open the Special Prices - Volume Discounts window, and
enter the quantity, discount, and special price.
After you enter or change the price, SAP Business One automatically calculates the discount according to the difference
between the quantity-based and the date-dependent special price.
 Note
In this window you can set different special prices for each of the defined units of measurement (UoM) of the item.
4. To confirm your entries, choose the Update button in the Special Prices - Volume Discounts window and the Period
Discounts window.
5. To save the modified special prices, choose Update in the Special Prices for Business Partners window.
 Note
To define quantity-based special prices, you do not have to define a date dependency in addition to the SAP Business
One default one. You can also define quantity-based special prices directly, based on the special price for the business
partner.

Special Prices for Business Partners Window
Overview of Special Prices for Business Partners
Item prices are usually defined in various price lists. The price list that is relevant for determining the prices for a particular
business partner is specified in the master data record of that business partner. A general discount can also be specified for the
business partner in the master data record. This discount is applied to the total of the item prices in the document.
However, it is often necessary to define special prices for individual cases. For example, you may require special prices for an item
or an item from an item group for a particular customer or vendor. You may also want to specify special prices or scaled discounts
for a particular customer that will be selected automatically by the system on the basis of the quantity ordered.
The logic behind the special prices and the procedure adopted by the system for calculating a price for an item are described in
this section.
Special Price Use
Special prices can be used for the following scenarios:
You want to specify a special price for a customer that purchases a particular item or an item from a particular item group.
In this case, you specify a price that depends on the business partner.
You want to define special prices for an item that are to apply for particular periods of time. In this case, you specify a date-
dependent price.
Depending on the quantity ordered, you want to assign a special price. If the quantity ordered is very large, you sell or buy
an item at a lower price than for a small quantity. In this case, you specify a quantity-based price.
From time to time, you will also want to update all or particular special prices. You can do this, for example, by changing the
discount for selected special prices. You can also select specific special prices and change only those prices. You can refer
price list updates to the derived special prices. You may also want to delete particular special prices after a defined period
of time.
Once you have defined special prices for individual cases (that is, for a particular business partner), you can copy them to
other business partners or groups of business partners according to various sets of rules.
If you want to assign discounts to particular item groups, items with particular properties, or manufacturers regardless of
the business partner, you can define discount groups.
If you do not want special prices to depend on a business partner, you can also define special prices for a price list. These
always apply if no special prices have been defined for a business partner. These special prices can also be defined on the
basis of a particular date and/or quantity.
Automatic Price Calculation
When you enter a business transaction, such as an outgoing invoice or a purchase order, the system calculates the price for an
item automatically. If a particular unit of measurement (UoM) is selected in the document's row, SAP Business One searches for
prices settings, for this particular UoM, in the different price sources by the following order:
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 163

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
1. The system first checks whether a special price has been defined for the particular UoM of the item for this particular
business partner. This special price could also be based on a particular date or quantity and can be defined for a particular
unit of measurement.
2. If no special price has been defined, the system checks whether a discount group that can be applied to the item has been
defined for the business partner or for the business partner group, ignoring the specific UoM selected in the document's
row.
3. If no special price has been defined, the system checks whether a special price has been defined for the item, for the
particular UoM (for the price list entered in the master record of the business partner), which once again can be based on a
particular date or quantity and can be defined for a particular unit of measurement.
4. If no special price has been defined, the system copies the price for the item from the price list entered in the master
record of the business partner, according to the particular unit of measurement.
 Note
If a price is not defined for the particular UoM that is selected in the document's row, SAP Business One searches for the prices
setting, for the inventory UoM of the item, by the same order mentioned above. The inventory UoM price from the highest
hierarchy is adjusted in proportion to the selected UoM, and displayed in the document's row.
If a discount has been granted because of a special price, the discount is indicated in the purchasing or sales document's row in
the Discount % field.

information.
Copy Special Prices to Selection Criteria Fields
Replace All Items/Replace Only Existing Items/Do Not Replace Items
Replace All Items
The application copies all special prices for the selected business partners and items. If a special price already exists for an
item, the existing price is overwritten. If no special price exists yet for an item, the special price is added.
Replace Only Existing Item
The application overwrites existing special prices of items in the target business partners. If a special price already exists
for an item, the existing price is overwritten. If no special price exists yet for an item, no special price is added.
Do Not Replace Items
The application adds new special prices for items without existing special prices in the target business partner. No changes
are made to existing special prices of items in the target business partners. If no special price exists yet for an item, the
special price is added.
 Example
Business partner A (BP A) and business partner B (BP B) both have items 4711 and 4712. Before the copy, 4711 has special price

Procedure
Change the Discount Percentage
1. Choose Inventory Price Lists Special Prices Update Special Prices Globally Change Discount % tab.
2. Enter a percentage figure in the Change Discount % of Items in Selection Criteria by field.
This determines the percentage that must be added to or subtracted from the current discount percentage as determined
in the items row in the Special Prices for Business Partners window. Enter a positive amount to increase the percentage
discount, or a negative amount to decrease the percentage.
3. Select the following, as required:
Automatic – select to update all items marked as automatic in the Special Prices for Business Partners window
(the Auto field is selected).
Not Automatic – select to update all items marked as not automatic in the Special Prices for Business Partners
window (the Auto field is deselected).
No Price List – select to update all items that are configured as Without Price List in the Special Prices for
Business Partners window (Without Price List is selected in the Price List field).
4. If you selected Not Automatic or No Price List, do one of the following:
Select Affects Price to make the change in the discount percentage affect the discount percentage per row and the
original Price After Discount.
Deselect Affects Price to make the change in the discount percentage affect the discount percentage per row and
the Price Before Discount, leaving the Price After Discount unchanged. This enables you to maintain a fixed price
after discount.
5. Choose OK.
Refresh by Price List
This option updates items that are associated with a price list but are not selected as automatic in the Special Prices for Business
Partners window (the Auto field is deselected). The price in the price list will be multiplied by the discount percentage set in the
Special Prices for Business Partners window, affecting the new special price.
1. Choose Inventory Price Lists Special Prices Update Special Prices Globally Refresh by Price List tab.

Update Special Prices Globally Window
Use this function to update all the special prices in SAP Business One.
Three different ways to update the selection criteria of special prices are:
Increase or decrease the discount percentage
Change the item prices by a percentage
Refresh special prices from their linked price list
Select the relevant tab to choose the operation required, define the change and the selection criteria, and click OK.
Example
The landlord of the Peaches and Cream fruit store has raised the rent for the store by 20%. Annie, the manager, must now raise
the prices of her produce by 7 %, which she has calculated will cover her increased costs. She backs up her company database
before she begins the update.
On the Change Discount % tab of the Update Special Prices Globally window, she types 7 in the Change Price of Items in
Selection Criteria by field and chooses OK. She does not select any specific business partner or items since she wants to raise
prices across the board.
To view the changes, she opens the Special Prices for Business Partners window; any business partner she selects displays the
updated prices. However, in the Price List window the original prices are evident.

In the Price Selectionsub-step, you specify the selection criteria from the price list perspective, that is, only the eligible prices in
the price lists will be updated later.
After you execute the update, only the eligible prices are updated in the price lists, and they are updated for the eligible items only.

Working with Item Prices in Sales and Purchasing Documents
In SAP Business One, when you create a sales and/or purchasing document, sometimes prices are automatically displayed in the
document. You may wonder how the prices are determined and where such prices are defined.
To help you to work with item prices in sales and purchasing documents, this topic describes the following information:
Price Sources and Discount Sources
How to Determine the Prices in Sales and Purchasing Documents
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 179

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
Price Sources and Discount Sources
In this topic, we demonstrate how prices in sales and purchasing documents are affected by price sources and discount sources.
The following diagram shows the relations between prices (in sales and purchasing documents) and price sources, as well as
prices and discount sources.
In sales and purchasing documents, prices are calculated according to the following formula:
Price after Discount = Item Price * (1 – Discount%)
For the item price in documents, a price can be taken from several windows, which are called price sources. The following price
sources are available:
Special Prices for Business Partners
Period and Volume Discounts
Price List
For the discount % in documents, a discount can be taken from several windows, which are called discount sources. The following
discount sources are available:
Special Prices for Business Partners
Discount Groups
The specific discount that is taken from the Discount Groups window is determined by the Effective Discount Groups field
defined on the Payment Terms tab of the Business Partner Master Data window.
Period and Volume Discounts
 Note
If you have enabled the separation between the net and gross price modes, item prices are taken to the document from
the price sources only when the document and the price source have the same price mode.
When Special Prices for Business Partner Is Used as the Price Source
Prerequisite:
No blanket agreement is linked to the document line
You have defined a special price that meets the following conditions:

partner and the line item selected in the sales or purchasing document.
The validity period defined in the Special Prices for Business Partners window includes the document posting date.

Price Source:
The price of the item defined in the Special Prices for Business Partners window is taken to the sales or purchasing
document line as the item price.
Discount Source:
The discount of the item defined in the Special Prices for Business Partners window is taken to the Discount % field in the
sales or purchasing document line.

The validity period defined in the Period and Volume Discounts window includes the document posting date.

Price Source:
In the sales or purchasing document, the item price is taken from the price list that is defined in the Form Settings window,
or is calculated after applying discount groups to the price list that is defined in the Form Settings window. You can also see
the price list number and price list name.
By default, the price list in the document Form Settings window is taken from the price list defined in the Business Partner
Master Data window. But it can be modified in the Form Settings window opened from the sales or purchasing document.
Discount Source:
If there is an available discount defined in the Discount Groups window, this discount will be taken to the Discount
% field in the sales or purchasing document line.
If there is no available discount defined in the Discount Groups window, no discount will be taken to the Discount %
field in the sales or purchasing document line.
How to Determine the Prices in Sales and Purchasing Documents
The determination rules of the item price in sales and purchasing documents are as follows:
If there is a blanket agreement linked to the sales or purchasing document, the item price will be taken from the linked
blanket agreement.
If there is no blanket agreement linked to the sales or purchasing document, the item price is determined by the option you
select in the Effective Price field on the Payment Terms tab of the Business Partner Mater Data window.

The document posting date falls within the validity period of price sources SP. Therefore, both the price source and the
discount source are taken from source SP.
Price after Discount = SP * (1 - SP%) = 100.00 * (1 - 10%) = 90.00
Case 2: Document posting date is 2018.06.15:
The document posting date falls within the validity period of price sources PV and discount source DG.
Price after Discount = PV * (1 - DG%)= 100.00 * (1 - 8%) = 92.00
Case 3: Document posting date is 2018.03.15:
The document posting date falls within the validity period of price sources PV and discount source PV.
Price after Discount = PV * (1 - PV%) = 100.00 * (1 - 5%) = 95.00
Case 4: Document posting date is 2018.09.15:
The document posting date falls within the validity period of price sources PL and discount source DG.
Price after Discount = PL * (1 - DG%) = 100.00 * (1 - 8%) = 92.00
Case 5: Document posting date is 2018.12.15:
The document posting date falls within the validity period of price sources PL.
Price after Discount = PV * 100% = 100.00 * 100% = 100.00

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
In the sales or purchasing document, the following information is defined or displayed:
In the Customer or Vendor field, C001 is selected
In the Item column in the document line, Computer is selected
In the document line, no blanket agreement is displayed
In the Form Settings window, Price List 01 is defined
When the Effective Price Considers All Price Sources checkbox on the Payment Terms tab of the Business Partner
Master Data window is not selected:
Case 1: Document posting date is 2017.04.01:
The document posting date falls within the validity period of the discount defined in the Discount Groups window. The
lowest price and the highest price are compared and taken from price A, B1 and B2.
A = SP * (1 - SP%) = 100.00 * (1 - 10%) = 90.00
B1 = PV * (1 - DG%) = 100.00 * (1- 8%) = 92.00
B2 = PL * (1 - DG%) = 100.00 * (1 - 8%) = 92.00
The lowest price is 90.00; the highest price is 92.00.
 Note
Price B1 and price B2 are the same, but price B1 will be taken as the highest price, because according to the default
priority, price B1 has a higher priority level than price B2.
Case 2: Document posting date is 2017.10.01:
The document posting date falls outside the validity period of the discount defined in the Discount Groups window. The
lowest price and the highest price are compared and taken from price A, C1 and C2.
A = SP * (1 - SP%) = 100.00 * (1 - 10%) = 90.00
C1 = PV * (1 - PV%) = 100.00 * (1- 5%) = 95.00
C2 = PL * 100% = 100.00 * 100% = 100.00
The lowest price is 90.00; the highest price is 100.00.
When the Effective Price Considers All Price Sources checkbox on the Payment Terms tab of the Business Partner
Master Data window is selected:
In both of the above cases, the lowest price and the highest price are compared and taken from all five prices.
A = SP * (1 - SP%) = 100.00 * (1 - 10%) = 90.00
B1 = PV * (1 - DG%) = 100.00 * (1- 8%) = 92.00
B2 = PL * (1 - DG%) = 100.00 * (1 - 8%) = 92.00
C1 = PV * (1 - PV%) = 100.00 * (1- 5%) = 95.00
C2 = PL * 100% = 100.00 * 100% = 100.00
Pick and Pack
This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 186

6/8/26, 6:09 AM
Pick and pack in SAP Business One lets you automate the processing of sales orders, A/R reserve invoices, production orders, and
inventory transfer requests in an orderly way, from the creation of pick lists up to packing items for shipment with delivery
documents.
The interactive graphics below help you navigate through this section. Choose the highlighted areas for more information.
Please note that image maps are not interactive in PDF outputs.
Prerequisites
Before you can begin working with pick and pack in SAP Business One, you need to have at least one open sales order, A/R reserve
invoice, production order, or inventory transfer request.
 Note
Sales orders created by business partners defined as a lead will not be displayed in the Pick Pack and Production Manager
window.
Example
The following is an example of a typical pick and pack flow in a company that maintains at least one warehouse.
Pick and Pack Scenario for Companies with Warehouse
1. In the company offices, one clerk or more handles the incoming orders and creates sales documents.
2. In the warehouse, an employee, possibly a designated pick dispatcher, accesses and filters the open sales orders, A/R
reserve invoices, production orders, and inventory transfer requests on his or her computer with the Pick Pack and
Production Manager window.
3. The pick dispatcher creates pick lists, prioritizing and grouping sales orders, A/R reserve invoices, production orders, and
inventory transfer requests by criteria such as required date or customer. The pick dispatcher checks released item
quantities against available item quantities and may decide to release pick lists for partial shipments.
4. The pick dispatcher allocates pick lists to employees who are designated as pickers. The pick dispatcher monitors the
processing of all pick lists using the different views and filters of the Pick Pack and Production Manager window.
5. Pickers pick the items from the warehouse shelves and mark the picked quantities in either printed or online pick lists.
6. Pickers or other employees create packages of items for shipment. Typically each shipment contains a delivery document
and a packing slip. Employees use SAP Business One to create and print these delivery documents.
Working with Pick and Pack

 Note
The selection you make in the Sort by dropdown list determines the order of the rows in the Pick Pack and Production
Manager window. This row order determines the distribution priority of the released quantities, as explained in the
following example.
 Example
If you sort the list by delivery date in the Delivery/Due Date fields, SAP Business One first allocates the available item
quantities to the rows with the earlier delivery date. This means that if the available quantities are inadequate for all
rows, those with a later delivery date will have a lower fulfillment.
SAP Business One calculates the available-to-release quantity specified in the Avail. to Release column for each row
according to the following:
The quantity in stock, minus the total released quantity, minus the total picked quantity, minus the total To Release
quantity.
7. Choose the OK button.
The Pick Pack and Production Manager window opens to the Open drawer view. For detailed information about the fields
in this window, see Pick Pack and Production Manager - Open Drawer.

2. Choose the Release to Pick List button.

Prerequisites
